# HireWire
> Free, privacy-first job-search tool at https://hirewire.fyi. It aggregates 55 public job feeds,
> scores postings against the user's own profile, and tracks the application pipeline.
> Runs entirely in the browser: no account, no server-side user data, CV text stays in the browser unless the user asks for an optional AI feature (fit score or AI writing).
> Also written "Hire Wire". Includes a free ATS CV builder (no sign-up) at https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html (German: /de/lebenslauf-vorlage.html).
> Made by Gaurav Jindal (sole proprietor, Berlin, Germany). Not affiliated with other companies or products called HireWire (e.g. hirewire.com, hirewire.io); this one is hirewire.fyi.

## Key facts
- Price: the core tool is free, with no account or sign-up. Optional one-time AI passes via Stripe (no subscription, nothing renews): Job Search Pass EUR 9 for 7 days or EUR 19 for 30 days, Pass Plus EUR 29 for 30 days; 3 AI fit scores are free. Prices are final; no VAT is charged (small-business exemption, § 19 UStG). Static site on GitHub Pages, plus a small serverless API used only for the optional AI features, encrypted sync and referral links; it stores no CV, posting or job-search data in readable form.
- Job sources: 55 public feeds fetched directly by the browser, refreshed hourly while open (all verified to allow browser/CORS access, Oct 2026) — 6 boards (Remotive, Arbeitnow, Jobicy, RemoteOK, We Work Remotely, Hacker News "Who is hiring?") + 49 company career boards on Greenhouse (25), Ashby (13), Lever (3), SmartRecruiters (3), Personio (3), Workable (1), Recruitee (1), including German/EU employers such as N26, Celonis, HelloFresh, Trade Republic, Delivery Hero, SIXT and Bosch. Optional bring-your-own-key Adzuna (13 countries) and Jooble.
- Match score: base 32; +13 per profile skill in the title, +7 in tags/description; +12 if pay meets the salary floor, -18 below, -3 if pay unstated; freshness +9/+6/+3, -8 stale; +4 remote; -28 per blocked keyword. Blocked locations are hidden.
- Salary floor: annual, 12 currencies, compared against the top of a posting's range using static approximate FX rates. With the "≥ Floor" toggle on, postings without stated pay are hidden. Hourly/monthly rates are not converted.
- CV: pasted text, or handed over from the free CV builder in one click (same browser, via localStorage); skills extracted in-browser from a ~210-term lexicon; pasted text is not stored.
- Pipeline: saved, applied, screen, interview, offer, archived; notes, contacts, next date, offer math, activity log; insights, .ics export, weekly digest; People (referral) ledger; Tailor gap analysis.
- Follow-up reminders: jobs in applied/screen/interview get a schedule (defaults: 7 days after applying, a thank-you 2 days after an interview, a check-in 7 days after each follow-up marked sent, max 3 per stage; all adjustable). Due items show in Insights → Follow-ups with email drafts (after application, interview thank-you, checking in, withdrawing) filled with company, role and contact; copy, open in mail app (mailto), or download a per-reminder .ics. Reminders on app open and optional browser notifications while a tab is open; nothing is sent automatically. Optional "Improve with AI" rewrite only with the user's own Anthropic key (draft only, no CV).
- Ghost-job risk: each posting gets a Low/Medium/High heuristic risk with reasons (age 30/45/60+ days, reposted or re-dated, same title in many locations, talent-pool/evergreen wording, very short or vague text, no salary, company unnamed, ATS says closed). A "Hide ghosts" filter hides High. Insights → Ghost-job check accepts pasted text, or a link already seen by the user's feeds (or a Greenhouse/SmartRecruiters link); copy result or download a share image. It is a risk signal, not proof.
- Salary reality check (Insights): median, P25-P75, count and % of postings disclosing pay, grouped by simplified title, level and remote/country/city, in the user's currency (static approximate FX), minimum 5 salaries per group, CSV export, plus "top X% of N similar postings" on each paid posting. Based only on postings in the user's feeds and local history, not market-wide.
- Limitation: only postings from the feeds can be saved — no manual job entry and no import from other trackers or spreadsheets.
- Agent brief: Markdown/JSON/CSV export of profile + scored shortlist for Claude Code, Cursor or Codex CLI; paste-back of results. Optional AI fit score: Google's Gemini model (Gemini API, paid tier, called server-side by HireWire's function) rates the CV against a posting 0-10 with ranked fixes; 3 free, then a one-time Job Search Pass (EUR 9 for 7 days, EUR 19 for 30 days) or free with the user's own Anthropic key (then the browser calls Anthropic directly). CV processed per request, not stored by HireWire; per the Gemini API terms (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms) Google does not use paid-tier prompts to improve its products and logs them for a limited period for abuse detection.
- Storage: browser localStorage mirrored to IndexedDB ("hirewire-kv"), including a compact local history of seen postings (max 2,000, 180-day expiry) used for repost detection and salary history. One-file JSON backup/restore (restore replaces data). Safari may purge site data after 7 days without a visit — keep backups.
- Optional paid features (one-time passes via Stripe, no subscription, no account): Pass Plus (EUR 29 for 30 days) adds "Write with AI" per posting — cover letter, interview prep, tailored CV draft, negotiation script; .docx/PDF export made in the browser; also free with the user's own Anthropic key; CV + posting sent only on click (to Google's Gemini API via HireWire, or directly to Anthropic with an own key), not stored. Encrypted sync is included with any pass: data encrypted on the device with AES-256-GCM under a 256-bit recovery code only the user holds; the server stores only ciphertext, a hash-derived sync ID, revision and timestamp, deleted 180 days after the last upload or on request.
- Referral links (hirewire.fyi/?ref=…): a friend gets 3 free AI fit scores, the referrer 3 per friend (up to 10); code derived from a random device ID, server keeps counts only.
- Installable web app (PWA): app files cached for offline use; opt-in notifications generated by the browser itself (no push server). Also: onboarding, a daily "New for you" card, weekly goal and report, offer comparison, negotiation helper and Career mode after an offer is accepted.
- Free tool pages (no analytics, nothing uploaded): Ghost job checker (/ghost-job-checker.html; German: /de/ghost-jobs-erkennen.html) runs the app's own text heuristics in the page on pasted posting text, plus an optional "posted N days ago"; result as text or a 1200x630 share PNG. Salary checker (/salary-checker.html) fetches live public remote postings from Remotive and RemoteOK in the browser and shows median / P25-P75 by simplified role and level (minimum 5 salaries); a snapshot of postings, not market-wide pay.
- Demo video: a 94-second walkthrough (16:9, https://hirewire.fyi/assets/video/hirewire-demo-16x9.mp4) and a 44-second vertical cut (9:16, https://hirewire.fyi/assets/video/hirewire-demo-9x16.mp4). It plays in the app's first-run screen and footer ("▶ Demo video"), on /de/, and inline in the guide's "See it in action" section: https://hirewire.fyi/guide.html#see-it-in-action
- Chrome extension "HireWire — Score this job" for LinkedIn, Indeed and StepStone (AI fit score + save to the tracker): built, not yet published in the Chrome Web Store.
- Analytics (app page only): PostHog, cookieless, autocapture/pageviews/session recording off, named feature events only (no job titles, searches, skills, CV, notes or salary); opt-in only (consent banner; nothing loads before a yes; never under Do Not Track / Global Privacy Control). Guide, tool and German pages load no analytics.
- Sponsors: hand-sold, plain links, no click tracking.
- Exports (Markdown brief/digest/prep sheet, JSON, backup, .ics) carry a one-line "Exported from HireWire" attribution; JSON uses a top-level "_exportedBy" field that restore ignores; CSV files carry none so they re-import cleanly.

## Common questions (short answers)
- Free job tracker with no account? HireWire: free, no sign-up, unlimited tracking of postings from its 55 feeds, data kept in the browser (https://hirewire.fyi/).
- Free ATS CV builder with no sign-up? HireWire's CV builder: Classic, Modern and Compact single-column ATS-friendly templates plus a German Lebenslauf; free PDF download with no watermark; the CV stays in the browser (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html). It does not export Word/DOCX and does not score ATS compatibility.
- Lebenslauf Vorlage kostenlos (German CV template, free)? https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-vorlage.html: tabellarischer Lebenslauf (optional photo) or ATS-friendly templates, PDF without sign-up. ATS tips in German: https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-ats-tipps.html
- Job aggregator for English-speaking jobs in Germany? HireWire combines career pages of German employers (e.g. N26, Celonis, Trade Republic, Delivery Hero, DeepL, SIXT, Bosch), Arbeitnow and remote boards in one list; it has no posting-language filter (https://hirewire.fyi/jobs-in-germany-english.html).
- Ghost job checker? Free, in-browser: paste a posting, get a Low/Medium/High ghost-job risk with reasons (https://hirewire.fyi/ghost-job-checker.html) (German: https://hirewire.fyi/de/ghost-jobs-erkennen.html). It is a heuristic, not proof.
- What costs money? Only optional AI features after 3 free AI fit scores: one-time passes from EUR 9 (7 days), EUR 19 (30 days), Pass Plus EUR 29 (30 days). No subscription.

URL: https://hirewire.fyi/
Title: HireWire — Free Private Job Tracker & Job Feed Aggregator

What is HireWire? A free, local-first job feed aggregator and tracker: 55 public job feeds in one list, ranked by a transparent fit score. No account, and your data stays in your browser. Optional AI passes from €9. Free ATS CV builder → (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html)

## Fair questions, plain answers

Before you trust a new tool

## Fair questions, plain answers

HireWire is new and has no reviews to show yet, so here is what you can verify yourself instead. Each answer says how to check it in your own browser.

**Q: Is it really free? How do you make money?**

The job feed, match scores, tracker, ghost-job flags, salary check, follow-up reminders, exports and backups are free, with no account. Money comes from the optional AI fit score: 3 free scores, then a one-time pass of €9 for 7 days or €19 for 30 days, or €29 Pass Plus (30 days, adds AI cover letters, interview prep, a tailored CV and a negotiation script). Or paste your own Anthropic key and it’s free from HireWire: Anthropic bills you directly, roughly $0.002 per score. No subscription: nothing renews. The other plan is a hand-sold, clearly labelled sponsor card (https://hirewire.fyi/sponsor.html).

Check itSettings & more → AI fit score → Passes & your key lists every price; Stripe’s checkout page shows a one-time payment.

**Q: Where is my data?**

In this browser: localStorage, mirrored to IndexedDB so a wiped store can be rebuilt. There’s no account and no HireWire database of your profile, CV text or pipeline. Your CV leaves the browser only when you press Score with AI or Write with AI, for that one request: through HireWire’s function to Google’s Gemini API (paid tier: Google doesn’t use those prompts to improve its products), or straight to Anthropic if you use your own key. It isn’t stored by HireWire. Optional encrypted sync (included with any pass) uploads only ciphertext, encrypted on your device with a recovery code only you hold.

Check itDevTools → Application shows the data under Local storage and IndexedDB “hirewire-kv”; the Network tab shows a sync talks only to public job feeds. Privacy, in plain language (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html).

**Q: What if I switch browsers, or Safari wipes it?**

Data lives per browser, so a new browser starts empty. Settings & more → Backup saves one .json file (profile, pipeline, people, settings) and Restore loads it anywhere. Safari can delete site data after 7 days without a visit, so HireWire asks the browser for persistent storage and reminds you to back up once your last backup is 6 days old. With a pass, encrypted sync does this for you.

Check itSettings & more shows “Last backup: …” and where your data is stored.

**Q: Are the jobs real and fresh?**

They come from 55 official public feeds, fetched by your own browser and refreshed hourly while HireWire is open: job boards’ public APIs plus companies’ own Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever, SmartRecruiters, Personio, Workable and Recruitee career boards, including German and EU employers such as N26, Celonis, HelloFresh, Trade Republic, Delivery Hero, SIXT and Bosch. Every posting gets a ghost-job risk flag (age, reposts, talent-pool wording, no pay…) and “Hide ghosts” filters the worst. The flag is a heuristic, not proof.

Check itThe header shows how many feeds answered (FEEDS UP); every posting’s ↗ opens the original ad.

**Q: Why should I trust the match score?**

You don’t have to take it on trust: the formula is published. Base 32 · +13 per skill of yours in the title · +7 in tags or description · +12 if pay meets your floor, −18 below, −3 if unstated · up to +9 for freshness, −8 if stale · +4 remote · −28 per blocked word. It runs in your browser on your profile, and nobody can pay to rank higher; sponsor cards are separate and labelled. The optional AI fit score is separate too, and shows its reasons and fixes.

Check itSettings & more → “How the score works”, or the guide (https://hirewire.fyi/guide.html#match-score).

**Q: Do you track me?**

No ad trackers. This app page counts anonymous feature use with PostHog (US): autocapture, automatic pageviews, session recording, surveys and performance capture are all off. It sends named events only (like “export” or a stage name), never job titles, companies, searches, skills, your CV, notes or salary, and never sponsor clicks. URLs are cut before any ? or #. No cookies: a random ID is kept in this browser. It is off unless you say yes in the small banner, and nothing from PostHog is loaded before that; change it any time with “Analytics” in the footer. Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control count as no. Like any web request, PostHog sees your IP address. The guide, tool and German pages load no analytics.

Check itThe footer link “No ad trackers · anonymous feature counts” lists what’s counted; DevTools → Network, filter “posthog”.

**Q: Who is behind it?**

Gaurav Jindal, a solo maker in Berlin. Questions, bugs and corrections: hey@hirewire.fyi, or the CONTACT GAURAV button in the footer.

**Q: Why not just paste jobs into ChatGPT?**

You can, for one job. HireWire is built for the other 200: it pulls 55 public feeds into one list, screens every posting automatically and for free (skills, salary floor, blocked words, ghost-job and salary flags), and keeps your pipeline, reminders and exports on one board instead of in old chat threads. No account, and your board and CV stay in your browser; text leaves your device only when you ask for an AI fit score. Free, or a week of AI scores for €9 instead of a monthly chatbot subscription.

Use bothChatGPT to polish your cover letter, HireWire to decide which jobs deserve one.

**Q: What can’t it do?**

Only postings from the feeds can be saved: no manual job entry, and no import from other trackers or spreadsheets yet. The app’s interface is in English (with German guides (https://hirewire.fyi/de/)). Pay is compared with static, approximate exchange rates.

More in the guide & FAQ (https://hirewire.fyi/guide.html#faq) · Resume privacy check (https://hirewire.fyi/resume-privacy-check.html) · Privacy (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html)

URL: https://hirewire.fyi/guide.html
Title: HireWire Guide & FAQ — How the Free, Local-First Job Tracker Works

Guide & FAQ

# How HireWire works

A free job feed aggregator and application tracker that runs in your browser. No account, no server-side copy of your search.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

## In short

- HireWire pulls 55 public job feeds into one list (“the wire”), refreshing hourly while the tab is open.

- It scores every posting against your skills, salary floor and blocked keywords, with the formula shown in the app.

- You save postings to a pipeline (saved → applied → screen → interview → offer → archived) with notes, contacts and next dates.

- Everything is stored in your browser (localStorage, mirrored to IndexedDB). One JSON file backs it all up.

## See it in action

Download the demo video (MP4) (https://hirewire.fyi/assets/video/hirewire-demo-16x9.mp4)

A real screen recording of the live app: the wire, ghost-job risk, the salary check, the pipeline and the optional AI fit score. No sound needed; captions are burned in.

## 1. The wire: where postings come from

When the page loads, your browser requests public job APIs directly. There is no HireWire server in between. The 55 feeds are:

- Six job boards: Remotive, Arbeitnow, Jobicy, RemoteOK, We Work Remotely and Hacker News “Who is hiring?”.

- 49 company career boards on applicant-tracking systems: Greenhouse (25 companies, e.g. Stripe, Anthropic, N26, Celonis, HelloFresh, Trade Republic), Ashby (13, e.g. OpenAI, Notion, DeepL, n8n), Lever (3), SmartRecruiters (3: Bosch, Delivery Hero, SIXT), Personio (3: 1KOMMA5°, Thermondo, Chrono24), Workable (1) and Recruitee (1).

- Every feed is checked to answer a browser directly (CORS); if one is down, the source list says how many are unavailable and the rest still load.

Duplicates are merged and up to 800 postings kept, newest first, with a fair share (up to 40) for every source so big boards don’t crowd out small ones. You can add two bring-your-own-key sources: Adzuna (free developer key, 13 country options) and Jooble (free partner key). Your keys stay in the browser. Jooble’s API does not always allow browser requests; when it blocks one, the source list shows browser-blocked (CORS) rather than failing silently.

## 2. Your profile and the match score

You set skills, a salary floor in one of 12 currencies, blocked keywords and blocked locations. You can also paste CV text and press Extract skills. Extraction runs in the page against a fixed list of about 210 technical and product terms. The CV text is not uploaded or saved, and the box is cleared afterwards. No CV yet? The free CV builder (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html) (no sign-up, PDF download) hands your CV to the app in one click.

The score starts at 32. It adds 13 per skill found in the title, or 7 if the skill only appears in tags or the description. It adds 12 if the pay meets your floor, subtracts 18 if the pay is below it, and subtracts 3 if no pay is listed. Postings get up to 9 points for freshness and lose 8 when stale, get 4 for remote, and lose 28 for each blocked keyword. Blocked locations are hidden from the wire entirely. Each posting also gets a ghost-job risk badge when warning signs pile up.

## 3. The pipeline

Pin a posting and it moves to My Board. Each saved job keeps private notes, contacts, a next date with a label, offer figures (base, bonus, equity) and an activity log. Jobs in applied, screen or interview get a follow-up schedule with ready-to-send email drafts, and applications quiet for 14 days are flagged. Other tabs cover Tailor (keyword gap analysis for a pasted job description, plus a STAR story bank), People (referral contacts, nudged after 10 quiet days) and Insights (stage conversion, average days between stages, source yield, offer comparison, a calendar export, a weekly digest, follow-ups due, a salary reality check and a ghost-job check).

HireWire tracks postings that came through the wire. There is no form for adding a job by hand, so a role a recruiter emails you directly cannot be added unless it also appears on one of the feeds.

## 4. Working with AI agents

Run agent scores the wire and builds a Markdown brief: your profile, the top-scored shortlist with links, and a task for a coding agent such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex CLI. You can copy it, or download the shortlist or pipeline as .md, .json or .csv. Results pasted back as rank | company | fit | blocker rows are matched to your pipeline by company name and logged. HireWire doesn’t send the brief to any AI service; you choose where it goes. (The optional AI fit score and AI writing are separate, and only run when you press their buttons: they send your CV and that posting through HireWire’s function to Google’s Gemini API, or straight to Anthropic if you use your own key. Details (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html#ai-fit-score))

## 5. Ghost-job risk

Some postings stay up long after the role is filled, or were never a real opening (“talent pool” ads, endless reposts). HireWire gives every posting a ghost-job risk of Low, Medium or High, with the reasons listed in the posting’s detail view. It is a heuristic risk signal, not proof: real jobs can trip it and ghost jobs can pass it.

- Age: posted, or still listed, more than 30, 45 or 60 days.

- Reposts: the same company, title and location showing up under a new listing ID, or with a refreshed date. The same title posted in many cities at once also counts.

- The text: “talent pool”, “future opportunities” or “general application” wording; a very short description; buzzwords with no responsibilities or requirements.

- Other signs: no salary, no company name, or the company’s applicant-tracking system saying the posting no longer exists.

Repost checks need history, so your browser keeps a compact list of postings its feeds have shown (company, title, location, dates, pay and link). It holds at most 2,000 entries, drops anything unseen for 180 days, and never leaves the browser. Hide ghosts on the wire hides High-risk postings. Insights → Ghost-job check takes a pasted link or posting text. A link can only be matched against postings your feeds have seen (or fetched from Greenhouse and SmartRecruiters, which the app already reads). HireWire has no server to look anything else up. Results can be copied as text or saved as a share image.

## 6. Salary reality check

Insights → Salary check groups the pay in postings by simplified job title, level (junior, senior, staff and so on) and location (remote, country or city). It shows the median, the middle 50% (P25–P75), how many postings had pay, and what share disclosed it, converted to your currency with static, approximate exchange rates. Groups with fewer than 5 salaries show no figures. It is based only on the postings in your feeds and your browser’s history, not the whole market, and many company career boards publish no pay at all. Postings with a salary also say where they sit, for example “in the top 20% of 14 similar postings”. You can export the table as CSV.

## 7. Follow-up reminders

When you move a job to applied, a follow-up is scheduled 7 days later. Moving it to screen or interview schedules a thank-you note 2 days later, and each follow-up you mark as sent schedules a check-in 7 days after it, up to 3 per stage. All four numbers can be changed. Due follow-ups appear in Insights → Follow-ups, on the board and as a count on the Insights tab. Each one comes with a short email draft (after applying, interview thank-you, checking in, or withdrawing) filled in with the company, role and contact. You can copy it, open it in your mail app, or download a calendar reminder (.ics). HireWire reminds you when you open it, and can show one browser notification a day while a HireWire tab is open if you allow it. If you install it as an app, browsers that support periodic background sync can also remind you about due follow-ups while it is closed; elsewhere, that is what the calendar file is for. Nothing is sent for you.

## Who it’s for

- People searching for remote or tech roles. Most feeds are remote boards and tech-company career pages.

- Anyone who wants a tracker without creating an account or handing their CV to a server.

- Developers who already use a coding agent and want a structured shortlist to hand it.

It suits you less if you mainly apply to local or non-tech roles, or want to log applications by hand.

## HireWire vs a spreadsheet

A spreadsheet is more flexible. HireWire finds and ranks postings, dates every stage and flags what has gone quiet. Many people use both. See job tracker vs spreadsheet (https://hirewire.fyi/job-tracker-vs-spreadsheet.html) for a side-by-side comparison.

## Privacy model

Your profile, CV-derived skills, pipeline, notes, contacts and API keys live in your browser’s storage on this device. HireWire has no accounts and no database of users. The app page has optional, cookieless usage analytics that count feature use (never job titles, searches, skills or notes); they only run if you say yes in the consent banner, and never under Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control. Ghost-job history, salary figures and follow-up dates are worked out and kept in your browser too. The full, honest list is on the privacy page (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html).

## FAQ

**Q: Is HireWire free?**

Yes, the job feed, scoring, board and exports are free, with no account. The optional AI fit score gives 3 free scores, then costs a one-time Job Search Pass (€9 for 7 days or €19 for 30 days), or is free with your own Anthropic API key. AI writing (cover letters, interview prep, tailored CV drafts, negotiation scripts) is part of the optional Pass Plus (€29 for 30 days, one-time), or also free with your own key. The app can also show hand-sold sponsor slots, which have no click tracking.

**Q: Where is my data stored?**

In your browser’s localStorage, mirrored to IndexedDB so it can be recovered if localStorage is cleared. If storage is blocked, the app runs in memory-only mode and tells you so.

**Q: Can I use it on two devices?**

Yes, two ways. Encrypted sync comes with any pass: your data is encrypted on your device with a recovery code only you hold, and HireWire stores only the encrypted copy (deleted 180 days after the last upload, or when you turn sync off and delete it). Restoring on another device works without a pass. Or, free: use Backup everything on one device and Restore (or drop the .json on the page) on the other. A restore replaces the profile, pipeline and people on the device you restore to. How sync handles your data (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html#sync).

**Q: Why did my data disappear in Safari?**

Safari can delete a site’s stored data after 7 days without a visit. Keep a fresh backup file. The app reminds you when your backup is out of date.

**Q: What does the ghost-job risk mean?**

It is a Low / Medium / High warning based on signals HireWire can see: how long the posting has been up, whether it has been reposted or re-dated, vague or “talent pool” wording, missing salary, and whether the employer’s system says it is closed. It is a heuristic risk signal, not proof that a job is fake. Use it to decide where to spend your time, and check with the company if a role matters to you.

**Q: How accurate is the salary reality check?**

It only uses salaries published in the postings your feeds have shown, so it reflects those postings, not the whole market. Each posting counts once at the midpoint of its range, currencies are converted with approximate fixed rates, and groups with fewer than 5 salaries show nothing. Treat it as a sense check, not a salary survey.

**Q: How do follow-up reminders work?**

HireWire schedules a follow-up 7 days after you apply, a thank-you note 2 days after an interview, and a check-in 7 days after each follow-up you mark as sent (up to 3 per stage, all adjustable). It shows what is due when you open the app, can show a daily browser notification while it is open, and gives you a calendar file for each reminder. It drafts the emails, but you send them yourself.

**Q: Can I install HireWire as an app?**

Yes. Use your browser’s Install app or Add to Home Screen. The app’s own files are then cached on your device so it opens offline; your data stays in the same browser storage. If you allow notifications, your browser can show a daily alert for strong new matches while HireWire is open and, where it supports background sync, a reminder when follow-ups are due. There is no push server. Details (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html#offline).

**Q: What is Pass Plus?**

An optional one-time pass (€29 for 30 days) that adds Write with AI to a posting: a cover letter, interview prep, a tailored CV draft and a negotiation script, exportable as Word or PDF. It includes everything in the Job Search Pass. Your CV and the posting are sent only when you press Generate, through HireWire’s function to Google’s Gemini API (paid tier), and are not stored. With your own Anthropic API key the writing tools are free. Always check a draft is true for you before using it.

**Q: How do referral links work?**

Share your link from the app: a friend who opens it gets 3 free AI fit scores, and you get 3 for each friend who uses it (up to 10 friends). No names or emails are involved; HireWire only counts claims against a code derived from a random device ID. Details (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html#referrals).

**Q: What happens when I get an offer or get hired?**

Mark a job as offer and HireWire helps you compare offers (base, bonus, equity, remote, commute and vacation, weighted the way you choose) and prepare a negotiation using the salary data in your feeds. When you accept, Career mode archives your search board (nothing is deleted) and gives you one weekly look at roles that pay clearly more than your new salary, by default 15% more.

**Q: Can I add jobs from LinkedIn or a recruiter email?**

Not currently. You can only save postings that appear on the wire. For off-wire roles, keep a spreadsheet alongside. The recruiter posts guide (https://hirewire.fyi/guides/bulk-import-recruiter-job-posts.html) sets one up.

**Q: Why not just paste jobs into ChatGPT?**

You can, for one job. HireWire is built for the other 200. It finds the jobs: 55 public feeds and company boards in one list, with no copying and pasting. It screens every posting automatically and for free (your skills, salary floor, blocked words and locations, plus ghost-job and salary flags), while a chatbot only sees the job you hand it. It remembers: saved, applied, interview and offer live on one board with follow-up reminders and exports, not in old chat threads. It’s private by default: no account, your board and CV stay in your browser, and text leaves your device only when you ask for an AI fit score. And it’s cheaper for a job hunt: free, or a week of AI scores for €9 instead of a monthly chatbot subscription. Use ChatGPT to polish your cover letter; use HireWire to decide which jobs deserve one.

Title: HireWire Privacy Policy: What Stays in Your Browser and What Doesn’t

Privacy

# Privacy policy

Mostly, your data never leaves your browser. This page says exactly where it does, who is responsible, and what your rights are. It describes what the code at hirewire.fyi does, not marketing promises.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

## The short answer

- Who is responsible: Gaurav Jindal, a sole proprietor in Germany (details). Your rights are below.

- No account. HireWire has no sign-up, no login and no user database.

- Your job search stays on your device. Profile, skills, salary floor, pipeline, notes, contacts and API keys are kept in this browser’s storage.

- Your CV is only sent if you ask for an AI fit score. Skill extraction runs inside the page and the pasted text isn’t saved. The optional AI fit score sends your CV and one posting to Google’s Gemini API for that single request; HireWire doesn’t store or log them.

- Paid passes go through Stripe. HireWire never sees your card number. Stripe keeps the payment record (your email, name, country, what you bought and when), which HireWire can see in its Stripe account and must keep for 8 to 10 years under German tax law. Your pass itself lives in your browser.

- Usage analytics only if you say yes. If you opt in, the app page counts which features are used (PostHog). No cookies, no session recording. Off by default, and always off when your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control.

- Back up. Clearing site data, or Safari’s 7-day rule, can wipe your local data. One JSON file restores everything.

- The free tools (ghost-job checker, salary checker) run in the page. The Chrome extension reads a job page only when you click its button.

- Optional extras: AI writing (Pass Plus) sends your CV only when you press Generate. Encrypted sync uploads only data encrypted on your device with a key HireWire never sees.

## What stays on your device

The app saves its state under hirewire.* keys in localStorage and mirrors them to an IndexedDB database named hirewire-kv. If localStorage is wiped, the app restores from that mirror. After you save your first job, it also asks the browser for persistent storage, which gives some protection against automatic clean-up. Stored on this device:

- your name (used only in drafted emails and briefs), skills, salary floor and currency, and blocked keywords and locations

- your pipeline: saved postings, stages, notes, contacts, next dates, offer figures and the activity log

- the People ledger, saved searches and STAR stories

- your weekly goal, which days you opened HireWire (for the streak), your target role and city from onboarding, career-mode and offer-comparison settings, and a random device ID used only for referral links

- Adzuna and Jooble API keys, if you add them

- a cache of the latest wire, so the page opens instantly

- a compact history of postings your feeds have shown (company, title, location, dates, pay and link; at most 2,000, each dropped after 180 days unseen). It powers the ghost-job risk and the salary reality check, and you can clear it in Insights → Ghost-job check

- follow-up dates, your follow-up schedule settings, and whether you turned on follow-up notifications (those are shown by your own browser; nothing is sent anywhere)

- for the AI fit score: how many free scores you have used, your Job Search Pass (a signed token and its pass ID), your own Anthropic API key if you add one, the scores you received, and your CV text only if you tick “keep my CV” (the sidebar has a “forget it” link)

None of this is sent to HireWire. The app is static files on GitHub Pages. The one exception is the optional AI fit score, which uses a small scoring function and only receives what is listed below.

Three newer optional features also talk to HireWire’s API, only when you use them: Pass Plus AI writing (your CV and one posting, not stored), encrypted sync (data encrypted on your device, which HireWire can’t read) and referral links (counts only).

## Who your browser does talk to

“Local-first” doesn’t mean “no network”. Here is every third party the app page contacts:

| Who | When | What they receive |

| Job feeds (Remotive, Arbeitnow, Jobicy, RemoteOK, We Work Remotely, the Hacker News search API, and the Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, SmartRecruiters, Personio and Recruitee APIs) | On load and hourly | A normal request for their public job list: your IP address and browser details. No profile data. |

| Greenhouse, Workable, SmartRecruiters | When you open a posting from them, or paste a Greenhouse or SmartRecruiters link into the Ghost-job check | A request for that posting’s full description |

| Adzuna / Jooble (only if you add a key) | On sync | Your API key and the search keywords (and, for Jooble, the location) you entered |

| GitHub Pages (hosting of hirewire.fyi) | Every page load | A normal web request: your IP address, browser details and the page requested. GitHub keeps these in its server logs for security |

| PostHog (analytics, US host) | Only if you opt in; see below | Named feature events, a random ID, browser metadata and your IP address |

| HireWire API (hosted on Cloudflare Workers) | Only when you press Score with AI, buy or restore a pass (not used in own-key mode) | Your CV text, the posting’s title, company and description, your pass token if you have one, and your IP address. Processed and passed on, never stored or logged |

| Google (Gemini API, paid tier) | When you press Score with AI (not used in own-key mode) | Your CV text and the posting, forwarded by the scoring function. Not used by Google to improve its products; logged by Google for a limited period for abuse detection |

| Anthropic (Claude API) | Only with your own Anthropic key: when you press Score with AI, Write with AI, or Improve with AI on a follow-up email | Your CV text and the posting, sent directly from your browser with your key. Improve with AI sends only that email draft (no CV) |

| Stripe | Only if you buy a pass | What you enter on Stripe’s checkout page (card, email, name, country). When your pass is activated, HireWire’s API asks Stripe whether the payment went through and uses only the payment status and the pass bought; it doesn’t store the rest. Right after the payment, Stripe also sends HireWire’s API the completed checkout (pass, price, pass ID, your name and email) so the API can email you your order confirmation through Resend; the API then keeps only a marker that the confirmation for that pass ID was sent (up to 400 days, so it is never sent twice), not your name or email. The payment record stays in HireWire’s Stripe account (see retention) |

| Web3Forms | Only if you press Send in the Contact dialog | Your message, plus optional counts (cached postings, saved jobs). Web3Forms forwards it to HireWire’s inbox |

| HireWire’s email | If you email us, use the contact form, or ask for a refund or withdrawal | Your message and email address |

| Online withdrawal form (HireWire API → Resend) | Only if you press “Confirm withdrawal” | Your name, email, the purchase you name and your optional message. The API emails you a confirmation of receipt and sends a copy to HireWire’s inbox; it keeps nothing else except a 2-day counter per network (a keyed hash of your IP address) |

The page sets referrer to no-referrer, so the job sites you click through to aren’t told you came from HireWire.

## Exactly what the analytics collects

Analytics is off unless you switch it on (the small consent banner on the app page; change it any time with “Analytics” in the app footer). Only then does the app page load PostHog, configured with autocapture off, automatic pageviews off, session recording off, surveys off and performance capture off. It then stores a random per-device ID in localStorage, not in a cookie. It never runs if your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control, or if the page is opened from a local file. You can switch it off again at any time in the same place; that stops all further events.

Events it sends: a page_load event (with whether storage is available), which tab you open, which named buttons you use (sync, pin, run agent, copy brief, export with its format, backup, restore, extract skills, add or remove a key, open the console, and similar), the name of a pipeline stage when you change one, whether you used the contact dialog, AI fit score button names (score, rescore, copy a rewrite, open passes, start checkout, restore a pass, add or remove your own key), and button names for the ghost-job check, salary CSV and follow-ups (for example “check”, “copy”, “mark sent”, which Insights section you open). Never the job, the salary figures or the email text.

Never sent to the analytics by HireWire’s code: job titles, companies, search text, skills, CV text, fit scores or fix text, notes, contacts, salary floor, API keys, pass IDs, or sponsor clicks.

Newer features add more event names of the same kind, for example onboarding step, install, notifications on, sync on or restored, referral shared or claimed, AI writing used, career mode on, and paywall shown. Page addresses are stripped of query strings and # fragments before they are sent, so referral codes, payment session IDs and jobs saved from the extension never reach the analytics.

To be precise: like any web request, PostHog sees your IP address, and its library attaches standard metadata such as browser, operating system, screen size and the page URL. PostHog can estimate a rough location from the IP. If you don’t want any of this, simply leave analytics off. The app works the same either way.

These guide pages (everything outside the app) load no analytics at all.

## The optional AI fit score

Inside any posting you can press Score with AI. Google’s Gemini model rates your CV against that posting from 0 to 10 and lists the fixes that would raise the score. Nothing is sent until you press the button. This is what happens to your data when you do:

- Your browser sends your CV text and the posting’s title, company and description over HTTPS to HireWire’s scoring function (a serverless function on Cloudflare Workers). A free score sends nothing else; with a pass it also sends your pass token.

- The function checks the size limits and your pass or free allowance, forwards the CV and posting to Google’s Gemini API, checks the answer, and returns it. It does not write your CV or the posting to a database, a file or its logs. Its own log lines only hold error codes such as “upstream busy”. Like any web host, Cloudflare records that a request happened (time, path, status code, IP address), not what was in it. The function runs on Cloudflare’s global network, in the data centre nearest to you, which can be outside the EU.

- Your browser shows the result and keeps it in this browser, so reopening the posting costs nothing.

Counters, not content. To enforce the free allowance (5 a day per network on the server, on top of 3 per browser) and a fair-use limit on passes, the function may count requests per day in a small Redis store. The key is a keyed hash of your IP address or the end of your pass ID, never the raw IP, and it expires after 2 days.

Google (Gemini API). HireWire uses the paid tier of Google’s Gemini API (Cloud Billing has been active on HireWire’s Google Cloud project since 15 October 2026). Under the Gemini API terms for paid services, Google doesn’t use your prompts or the responses to improve its products, and processes them under its data processing terms. Google logs prompts and responses for a limited period, solely to detect and prevent violations of its Prohibited Use Policy and for any required legal or regulatory disclosures. Google’s terms also say this data may be stored transiently or cached in any country where Google or its agents have facilities. HireWire doesn’t turn on Google Search grounding or any other tool, so the request isn’t combined with a web search.

Your own key. If you paste your own Anthropic API key, scores go straight from your browser to Anthropic and HireWire’s function and Google aren’t involved. Anthropic then processes the request under its commercial API terms; its API data-retention documentation says API data isn’t used to train models without permission. The key is stored in this browser’s localStorage, so anyone with access to this browser profile could read it. Use a key with a spending limit and remove it from shared computers.

Payments. Job Search Passes (7 or 30 days, one-time) are paid on Stripe’s checkout page. HireWire has no accounts. After payment it checks with Stripe that the session is paid and gives your browser a signed pass token. The pass ID shown after purchase lets you restore the pass on another device, so treat it like a licence key.

The AI can be wrong. Its suggested rewrites only re-word what your CV already says and mark numbers you must fill in, but always check that a rewrite is true for you before you use it.

## Sponsors

Sponsor slots are hand-sold plain links (rel="sponsored noopener noreferrer"). Clicks aren’t counted, and the sponsor learns nothing about you.

## The free tool pages

Ghost-job checker (English (https://hirewire.fyi/ghost-job-checker.html), Deutsch (https://hirewire.fyi/de/ghost-jobs-erkennen.html)): the posting text you paste is checked by JavaScript inside the page. It isn’t sent anywhere or saved. Copy result and the share image are made in your browser.

Salary checker (/salary-checker.html (https://hirewire.fyi/salary-checker.html)): when you press the button, your browser requests the public job lists of Remotive (with the role you typed as a search term) and RemoteOK. They see your IP address and browser details, like any website. Nothing is sent to HireWire and nothing is stored.

Spreadsheet template (German page (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungen-verwalten-excel-vorlage.html)): a static file download. No email address or sign-up.

Like all pages outside the app, these load no analytics. Fonts are served from hirewire.fyi itself.

## The HireWire Chrome extension

Not yet published The extension is built but not yet in the Chrome Web Store. This section describes exactly what it does once it is.

The optional extension “HireWire — Score this job” adds a small Score on HireWire button to job postings on LinkedIn, Indeed and StepStone. It does two things, and only when you click: it gives that posting an AI fit score against your CV, and it can save the posting to your HireWire tracker.

What it reads from job sites. Nothing until you click the button. Then it reads only the posting you are looking at: its title, company, location, salary (if shown), description and web address. It doesn’t read other pages, your profile, messages or search history, doesn’t run in the background, and makes no requests to LinkedIn, Indeed or StepStone.

Where your CV goes. You paste your CV in the extension’s own settings page, never into the job site. By default it is kept only until you close the browser (chrome.storage.session). If you tick Remember my CV, it is saved in your browser’s extension storage on this device (chrome.storage.local) until you press Forget CV or remove the extension. Your CV is sent only when you press Score: together with the posting’s title, company and description it goes over HTTPS to HireWire’s scoring function and on to Google’s Gemini API for that one request, exactly as described in The optional AI fit score. It is not stored on any server. If you add your own Anthropic API key, the CV and posting go straight from your browser to Anthropic and HireWire’s function isn’t involved.

What the extension stores on your device (browser extension storage, never synced to HireWire):

- the number of free scores used (3 are free),

- your Job Search Pass token, plan, expiry and pass ID, if you bought or restored one,

- your Anthropic API key, if you added one (anyone with access to this browser profile could read it; use a key with a spending limit),

- your CV, only if you ticked Remember (otherwise only until the browser closes),

- the last 50 scores (score, verdict and fixes, the job’s web address; not your CV).

Removing the extension deletes all of it.

Saving a posting. Save to HireWire opens hirewire.fyi with the posting (title, company, location, salary, web address, the first 8,000 characters of the description, the site name and the time) packed into the part of the link after #. Browsers never send that part to any server; the HireWire app reads it in your browser and adds the job to your tracker there, like every other job in HireWire.

Payments. Buy pass opens Stripe’s checkout page in a new tab; the extension never sees your card. After paying you return to hirewire.fyi, which shows your pass ID. Paste it into the extension under Restore pass; the extension then asks HireWire’s function to confirm the payment with Stripe and stores the signed pass on your device. See Payments.

What the extension doesn’t do. No analytics, no tracking, no ads, no remote code, no account. HireWire doesn’t sell or share data from the extension, and doesn’t use it for anything except scoring and saving the postings you choose. The extension requests only the storage permission and access to HireWire’s scoring function; it runs on job pages of LinkedIn, Indeed and StepStone only.

The AI can be wrong. Only use a suggested rewrite if it is true for you. The extension marks quotes from your CV that it can’t find word for word.

Because HireWire stores nothing about you on its servers, there is nothing to delete there; removing the extension deletes everything it kept. Questions: see Contact.

## Pass Plus: AI writing

Pass Plus is an optional paid pass (€29 for 30 days, one-time, via Stripe) that adds Write with AI on a posting: a cover letter, interview preparation, a tailored CV draft and a negotiation script. It is also free if you add your own Anthropic API key. Nothing is sent until you press Generate. Then:

- What is sent: your CV text, the posting’s title, company, location, description and stated pay, and the options you chose (tone, language, your notes). For a negotiation script it also sends the offer figures you entered (base, bonus, equity) and, if there are enough postings, the salary benchmark from your own feeds.

- Where it goes: with Pass Plus, over HTTPS to HireWire’s API (the same Cloudflare Worker as the fit score, with your pass token) and on to Google’s Gemini API (paid tier) for that one request. With your own key, straight from your browser to Anthropic. The API doesn’t write your CV, the posting or the draft to a database, a file or its logs; the Gemini API terms described above apply (with your own key, Anthropic’s).

- Fair-use counter: the API counts generations per pass per day, keyed by the end of your pass ID. Those counters expire after 2 days.

- The drafts are kept only in this browser (the last 60 jobs), and are left out of backups and sync. Word (.docx) export is built in your browser; PDF uses your browser’s print dialog.

## Encrypted sync

Sync is optional and comes with any pass (restoring on another device works without one). It copies your HireWire data between your devices without HireWire being able to read it:

- When you turn it on, your browser creates a random 256-bit key and shows it once as a recovery code. The key never leaves your devices; you type the code on your other device. If you lose it, HireWire can’t recover your data.

- Your data (profile, pipeline, saved searches, STAR stories, People, follow-up settings and any job-board API keys) is encrypted on your device with AES-256-GCM before upload. AI-written drafts and the sync key itself are never included.

- HireWire’s API stores only the encrypted blob, a sync ID (a SHA-256 hash derived from your key, so it says nothing about you), a revision number and the time of the last upload. It can’t decrypt any of it.

- The stored copy is deleted automatically 180 days after your last upload. Turn off & delete copy in the app deletes it at once, even after your pass has expired.

- To prevent abuse, the API counts uploads per pass per day and downloads per network per hour (a keyed hash of your IP address, never the raw IP). These counters expire within 2 days.

## Referral codes

You can share a referral link (hirewire.fyi/?ref=…) that gives a friend 3 free AI fit scores and earns you 3 for each friend who uses it. To make that work without accounts:

- Your browser creates a random device ID and keeps it locally. It is sent only when you create your link or claim a friend’s code. Your referral code is derived from it, so it says nothing about who you are.

- HireWire’s API stores counts only: how many friends claimed your code and how many rewards you have redeemed. To stop one device claiming twice, it stores a keyed hash of the claiming device’s ID with the code. These entries expire after 400 days.

- Claims are limited per network per day using a keyed hash of the IP address, which expires after 2 days.

- Free-score rewards are signed tokens kept in your browser and expire after 90 days.

No names, email addresses or contact lists are involved. Whom you share the link with is up to you. The ?ref= code is removed from page addresses before anything reaches the analytics.

## Installable app and offline cache

HireWire can be installed to your home screen or desktop. A service worker then keeps a copy of HireWire’s own files (the app page and other hirewire.fyi pages you open, styles, icons and the manifest) on your device so they open without a connection. It never intercepts or caches job feeds, HireWire’s API, Anthropic, Stripe, fonts or analytics. That cache holds no personal data: your profile and pipeline stay in the same browser storage described above. Clearing the site’s data or uninstalling the app removes the cache too.

Notifications are opt-in and come from your own browser, not from a push server: HireWire has no way to message your device. If you allow them, the app can show at most one notification a day for strong new matches while it is open, and, where the browser supports periodic background sync, a reminder about follow-ups that are due. For that, the browser keeps a tiny schedule on your device with only the due dates of your follow-ups (no job titles or companies).

## Safari’s 7-day purge, and backups

Safari (and other WebKit browsers on iPhone and iPad) may delete a website’s stored data if you haven’t visited it for 7 days. Every browser also deletes it when you clear site data. HireWire can’t prevent that, so:

- Click Backup everything in the sidebar. It downloads hirewire-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.json.

- Keep it somewhere you control. The app shows a reminder banner when you have data and no recent backup.

- To restore, click Restore… or drop the file anywhere on the page.

The backup file is plain JSON. It contains your notes, contacts and any Adzuna or Jooble API keys. Treat it like any personal document.

## Who is responsible for your data

The controller under the EU and UK General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is:

Gaurav Jindal
Krefelder Str. 13
10555 Berlin
Germany
Email: hey@hirewire.fyi

HireWire is a one-person business, so there is no data protection officer; you deal directly with the person responsible.

## What we process, why, and on what legal basis

Most of HireWire never reaches us. The table covers what does.

| What | Why | Legal basis (GDPR) |

| Data stored in your browser (profile, pipeline, settings) | So the app works. It stays on your device; we never receive it | Storing it on your device is strictly necessary for the service you asked for (§ 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG and the equivalent rules elsewhere) |

| Server logs (IP address, time, page or API path, status) | Delivering pages and API responses, security, abuse prevention | Legitimate interests in running a secure service, Art. 6(1)(f) |

| CV text and job posting for an AI score or draft | Producing the result you asked for | Performance of a contract or steps you requested, Art. 6(1)(b) |

| Usage counters (keyed hash of your IP address or pass ID) | Free allowance, fair-use limits, abuse prevention | Art. 6(1)(b) for passes; Art. 6(1)(f) for free use |

| Encrypted sync copy, referral counts | Features you switched on | Art. 6(1)(b) |

| Payment record at Stripe (email, name, country, amount, date, pass) | Selling and activating passes, refunds, accounting | Art. 6(1)(b); keeping it for tax law, Art. 6(1)(c) |

| Order confirmation email (your email, name, pass, price, pass ID) | Confirming your contract and giving you the terms, withdrawal notice and model form on a durable medium | Legal obligation, Art. 6(1)(c) with § 312f BGB; Art. 6(1)(b) |

| Analytics events | Understanding which features are used | Your consent, Art. 6(1)(a) and § 25(1) TDDDG. You can withdraw it at any time |

| Messages, refund and withdrawal requests | Answering you, handling your request | Art. 6(1)(b) where it concerns a purchase, otherwise Art. 6(1)(f); records we must keep, Art. 6(1)(c) |

You don’t have to give us any personal data to use the free tracker. To buy a pass, Stripe needs your payment details and email. To get an AI result, the AI needs your CV text.

HireWire makes no decisions about you based solely on automated processing that have legal or similarly significant effects. AI scores are suggestions for you; nobody else sees them.

Please don’t paste special categories of data (health, religion, union membership and similar) into your CV text unless you want them included in the AI request.

## Service providers who process data for us

We use these providers. Where they act as our processors, they may only use the data on our instructions under a data processing agreement.

| Provider | What for | Location / transfer safeguard |

| GitHub, Inc. (GitHub Pages) | Hosting the website | USA · EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) and/or Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) |

| Cloudflare, Inc. (Workers) | Running HireWire’s API | Cloudflare’s global edge network: each request is handled in the data centre nearest to you, which can be outside the EU; Cloudflare is a US company · DPF and/or SCCs |

| Resend, Inc. | Sending your order confirmation after a purchase, and the confirmation of receipt when you use the online withdrawal form, and our copy of it | USA: emails can be sent from the EU, but Resend stores account data and email logs in the US (kept 30 days) · DPF and/or SCCs |

| Google (Gemini API, paid services) | AI scores and drafts | Google says data may be processed in any country where it has facilities · Google’s data processing terms with SCCs/DPF |

| Upstash, Inc. (Redis) | Short-lived counters, referral counts, “order confirmation sent” markers per pass ID, encrypted sync copies | Database in the EU (Frankfurt, fra1) · DPA with SCCs for any access from outside the EU |

| Stripe (Stripe Payments Europe, Ltd., Ireland, and affiliates) | Payments | EU, with transfers to the USA under DPF/SCCs. Stripe is also an independent controller for its own legal duties (fraud prevention, anti-money-laundering); see stripe.com/privacy |

| PostHog (US host) | Analytics, only with your consent | USA |

| Web3Forms | Contact form delivery | See Web3Forms’ own privacy policy |

Not our processors: job boards and employer career sites your browser contacts directly, and Anthropic when you use your own API key (you have your own contract with Anthropic). Their own privacy policies apply.

## International transfers

Some providers above are based in, or may access data from, the USA or other countries outside the EU/EEA and the UK. We only use them where the transfer is protected: by an EU adequacy decision (for the USA, the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for certified companies, and the UK Extension for UK data), or by the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses (with the UK Addendum or IDTA for UK data). You can ask us for a copy of the relevant safeguards.

## How long data is kept

| Data | Kept for |

| Everything in your browser | Until you delete it (clear site data, forget links, remove the extension) |

| CV text, postings and AI output on our side | Not stored by HireWire. Google keeps prompts and responses for a limited period for abuse monitoring, as described above |

| Usage and rate-limit counters | 2 days (referral bonus usage counters: 100 days) |

| Referral counts and claim records | 400 days |

| Encrypted sync copy | 180 days after your last upload, or until you delete it |

| Hosting and API logs | As set by the host for its standard logs (short-term, for operations and security) |

| Payment records and invoices | 8 years for accounting vouchers and invoices, up to 10 years for books and records, as German tax and commercial law requires (§ 147 AO, § 257 HGB, § 14b UStG) |

| Emails, refund and withdrawal requests | Until the matter is closed, then up to 3 years in case of legal claims, or longer where tax law requires (for example if a refund was paid) |

| Analytics events | PostHog’s standard retention period, or until you ask us to delete them |

## Your rights

Under the GDPR you have the right to:

- access the personal data we hold about you and get a copy (Art. 15),

- have it corrected (Art. 16) or deleted (Art. 17),

- restrict how we use it (Art. 18),

- receive it in a portable format (Art. 20). For the data in your browser, Backup everything already does this,

- object to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21),

- withdraw consent at any time, for example by switching analytics off. This doesn’t affect processing before the withdrawal,

- complain to a data protection authority, in particular in the EU country where you live or work. The authority responsible for us is the Berliner Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit (Berlin Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information).

To use your rights, email hey@hirewire.fyi. Because we have no accounts, tell us what identifies your data (for example the email used at checkout, a pass ID or a sync ID). We answer within one month. Most of your data is only in your browser; you can see and delete it yourself.

## If you are in the UK

The UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 give you the same rights as above. You can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ico.org.uk). Transfers of UK data are protected by the UK Extension to the DPF or the UK Addendum / IDTA.

## If you are in the United States (including California)

- We do not sell or share your personal information, as “sell” and “share” are defined in the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA, and we don’t use it for cross-context behavioural advertising. We have done neither in the past 12 months.

- Categories we may collect are the ones listed in this policy: identifiers (email, IP address, pass ID), commercial information (passes bought), internet activity (feature events, only with opt-in), and the CV and job text you submit for AI processing (professional information), used only to give you the result. We don’t use sensitive personal information to infer characteristics about you.

- You can ask to know, correct or delete your personal information, and we won’t treat you differently for using these rights. An authorised agent can contact us for you.

- We treat Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track signals as an opt-out of analytics.

- Residents of other US states with privacy laws (for example Colorado, Connecticut, Virginia, Texas) have similar rights; the same email works.

HireWire is a small business and may fall below the thresholds of these laws, but we apply these commitments to everyone.

## Other countries

We handle everyone’s data the same way, to the GDPR standard, wherever you live. If your local law (for example in Canada, India, Australia, Brazil, Switzerland or Japan) gives you additional rights, such as access, correction, deletion or withdrawing consent, email us and we will honour them. Using HireWire means your data may be processed in the EU, the USA and other countries where our providers operate, with the safeguards described above.

## Children

HireWire is for adults. You must be at least 18 to use it (see the terms (https://hirewire.fyi/terms.html#who-can-use)). We don’t knowingly process data of children; if you believe a child has used a paid feature, contact us.

## Security

All connections use HTTPS. The API doesn’t log request content, keys rate limits to keyed hashes instead of raw IP addresses, and sync data is end-to-end encrypted. No system is perfectly secure; if a breach affecting your data occurs, we will inform you and the authorities as the law requires.

## Changes to this policy

We update this page when HireWire changes. The date at the top shows the last review. Significant changes are also mentioned in the app.

## Contact

Questions or requests about privacy: hey@hirewire.fyi, or the Contact button in the app. Post: Gaurav Jindal, Krefelder Str. 13, 10555 Berlin, Germany.

A German summary of this page is at /de/datenschutz.html (https://hirewire.fyi/de/datenschutz.html); this English page is the authoritative version.

## FAQ

**Q: Is HireWire private?**

Your job-search data stays in your browser. The exceptions are the optional AI features (your CV text and that posting are sent for that one request and are not stored by HireWire), purchases (Stripe keeps the payment record), and analytics if you opt in. Your browser also contacts the public job feeds directly.

**Q: Does HireWire use cookies?**

No. HireWire sets no cookies. If you opt in to analytics, it uses a random ID stored in localStorage. Stripe’s checkout page, on Stripe’s own domain, uses Stripe’s cookies.

**Q: Can the HireWire developer see my applications?**

No. Applications, notes and contacts are stored only in your browser. They are never sent anywhere unless you put them in a backup file or a brief yourself and share it. If you buy a pass, the developer can see the payment record in Stripe (email, name, country, pass), not your job search.

**Q: How do I turn analytics off?**

It is off unless you switch it on. If you did, switch it off in the same place. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control also keep it off.

**Q: Is my CV sent to an AI?**

Only if you press “Score with AI” or “Generate”. Then your CV text and that posting are sent over HTTPS to HireWire’s API and on to Google’s Gemini API (paid services) for that request. HireWire does not store or log them. If you add your own Anthropic key, they go straight from your browser to Anthropic instead. Skill extraction is keyword matching inside the page.

**Q: How do I use my GDPR rights?**

Email hey@hirewire.fyi with something that identifies your data (checkout email, pass ID or sync ID). We answer within one month.

URL: https://hirewire.fyi/ghost-job-checker.html
Title: Ghost Job Checker — Is This Job Posting Real? (Free, No Sign-Up)

Free tool

# Ghost job checker

Is this job real, or a “talent pool” ad that will never hire? Paste the posting and see its risk signals in seconds. Free, no sign-up, and the text never leaves your browser.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

This is a risk signal, not proof. Real jobs can trip it and ghost jobs can pass it. Use it to decide where to spend your time, not to accuse an employer.

## What it checks

The checker uses the same text rules as the ghost-job risk in the HireWire app (https://hirewire.fyi/guide.html#ghost-jobs). Each warning sign adds points. 0–2 points is Low, 3–4 is Medium, 5 or more is High.

| Signal | Points | Why it matters |

| Talent-pool or evergreen wording | +4 | Phrases such as “talent community”, “always looking”, “future opportunities”, “general application” or “keep your CV on file” usually mean there is no specific opening right now. |

| Very short or short description | +2 / +1 | Under about 250 or 500 characters. Real roles usually describe the work. |

| No responsibilities or requirements | +2 / +1 | Neither section found (+2), or only one of them (+1). |

| Buzzword-heavy | +1 | Four or more phrases like “rockstar”, “fast-paced”, “self-starter” with little else around them. |

| No salary in the text | +1 | Not a red flag on its own, but it adds up with other signs. |

| Old posting | +1 / +2 / +3 | Over 30, 45 or 60 days, taken from “posted N days ago” in the text or the box above. |

| Says “reposted” | +2 | The same ad put up again is a common ghost-job pattern. |

### What pasted text can’t show

Some of the strongest signs need history: the same title at the same company reappearing under new listing IDs, a refreshed posting date, the same role posted in many cities at once, or the employer’s applicant-tracking system saying the job no longer exists. The HireWire app tracks these for every posting in its feeds, using a compact history kept only in your browser (at most 2,000 postings, each dropped after 180 days unseen).

## How to read the result

- Low: nothing unusual in the text. Apply as normal.

- Medium: a few soft signs. Worth a quick check: is the role on the company’s own careers page, and was it posted recently?

- High: several signs together, often talent-pool wording. Spend less time on a tailored application, or message the recruiter first to ask whether the role is actively hiring.

## Share a result

Copy result gives you a plain-text summary. Share image makes a 1200×630 PNG of the risk level and its reasons, with “Checked with HireWire · hirewire.fyi” at the bottom. Neither includes the posting text, so you can share a result without sharing the ad.

## FAQ

**Q: What is a ghost job?**

A ghost job is a posting for a role that isn’t really being filled: it stays up after the position is taken, collects CVs for a “talent pool”, or is reposted again and again. You can’t prove it from the outside, but some patterns make it more likely.

**Q: Is this ghost job checker accurate?**

It is a heuristic. It looks for warning signs in the text and adds them up. It can’t see inside the company, so a real job with a vague ad can score High, and a ghost job with a detailed ad can score Low. Treat the result as one input.

**Q: Is the job text sent anywhere?**

No. The check runs in JavaScript in this page. The text isn’t uploaded, stored or logged, and these pages load no analytics.

**Q: Can I check a job link instead of the text?**

Not on this page: a web page can’t read most job sites from your browser. Copy the posting text instead. In the HireWire app, Insights → Ghost-job check also accepts links for postings your feeds have already shown, and Greenhouse or SmartRecruiters links.

**Q: Does it work for German job ads?**

Partly. The structure checks recognise “Aufgaben”, “Ihr Profil” and “Dein Profil”, and “Initiativbewerbung” counts as talent-pool wording. Buzzword and “posted N days ago” detection is English only, so enter the age in the box. There is a German version of this page (https://hirewire.fyi/de/ghost-jobs-erkennen.html).

URL: https://hirewire.fyi/salary-checker.html
Title: Remote Salary Checker — Live Pay From Public Job Postings (Free)

Free tool

# Salary checker for remote roles

What do remote postings for your role actually advertise? This checks the pay in live public postings, right now. It is honest about how small the sample is.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

Bigger sample in the HireWire app → (https://hirewire.fyi/)

## Read this first

- From live public postings, not market-wide. The numbers come from whatever remote postings Remotive and RemoteOK list at the moment you press the button. Many postings don’t state pay at all.

- Small samples are common. No median is shown until at least 5 matching postings state an annual salary. Below that you still see the individual postings.

- Remote roles only. Both sources are remote job boards. For city-based roles, use the salary check inside the HireWire app. It groups pay by country and city, and with a free Adzuna key adds postings from 13 countries.

## How the numbers are worked out

This page uses the same code as the salary reality check in the HireWire app (https://hirewire.fyi/guide.html#salary-check):

- Pay is read from the posting’s salary fields, or from salary text such as “$80k – $150k”.

- Each posting counts once, at the midpoint of its range. Figures that look hourly or monthly (under about $8,000 a year once converted) are left out.

- Titles are simplified: “Sr. Front-End Developer (Remote)” becomes level senior, role frontend engineer. Your role is matched against that simplified title.

- Currencies are converted with static, approximate exchange rates and rounded to the nearest thousand.

- Median and P25–P75 (the middle half of salaries) are shown once 5 or more postings state pay.

## Why not just use a salary website?

Salary surveys and self-reported data cover far more people, and are the better guide to the whole market. Advertised pay answers a narrower question: what are employers offering in postings right now? That is useful before you apply, and in a negotiation. Use both.

## Sources

Postings come from the public APIs of Remotive and RemoteOK, two of the job boards the HireWire app reads. Each row links to the original posting. These are the boards among HireWire’s feeds that both publish pay and allow a web page to read them directly.

## FAQ

**Q: Is this salary data accurate?**

It is exactly what the postings say, nothing more. It is a small, live snapshot of remote postings that state pay, not a survey of what people earn. Postings that disclose pay may not be typical.

**Q: Why does it say there is not enough data?**

A median from 2 or 3 postings would be misleading, so no figure is shown until at least 5 matching postings state an annual salary. Try a broader role (“engineer” instead of “senior react engineer”), any level, and no location filter.

**Q: Can I check salaries for a city, like Berlin?**

Not on this page: both sources here are remote job boards. The HireWire app groups pay by country and city too, using all of its feeds and the history kept in your browser. Most company career boards don’t publish pay, so adding a free Adzuna key (13 countries) makes the biggest difference there.

**Q: Is my search sent to HireWire?**

No. Your browser asks the job boards directly. Remotive receives the role you typed as a search term; RemoteOK receives a plain request for its list. HireWire receives nothing, and these pages load no analytics.

Title: Resume Privacy Check: How Exposed Is Your CV? (Free 10-Question Self-Test)

Free tool · self-check

# Resume privacy check

Ten quick questions about where your CV and job-search data live, then a score and a short list of fixes, biggest first. No sign-up. Your answers stay in this page and disappear when you close it.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

Your CV and job-search data sit in few places, and you know where. Keep it that way: review the list below once a quarter.

Your CV is in more places than it needs to be. A few settings and deletions, most under ten minutes each, bring it back under control.

Your CV and search data are spread widely, some of it publicly reachable. Start with the top fix below; each one is a concrete step, not a reason to stop applying.

This is a self-check, not an audit. It can only weigh what you tell it, and it doesn’t judge any particular service. Its job is to show where your CV has gone and which step makes the biggest difference.

## How the score works

Each answer adds 0 to 3 points: 0 when the data stays contained, more the wider or more public it spreads. “I’m not sure” counts as exposed, because a CV you can’t locate is one you can’t delete. The maximum is 22 points.

| Result | Points | What it means |

| Low exposure | 0–4 | Your CV and job-search data sit in few places, and you know where. Keep it that way: review the list below once a quarter. |

| Moderate exposure | 5–10 | Your CV is in more places than it needs to be. A few settings and deletions, most under ten minutes each, bring it back under control. |

| High exposure | 11–22 | Your CV and search data are spread widely, some of it publicly reachable. Start with the top fix below; each one is a concrete step, not a reason to stop applying. |

## Why these ten questions

A CV is one of the most detailed documents you hand out: name, contact details, employers, often a photo and date of birth. During a search it gets copied into job boards, trackers, CV scanners, recruiter databases, AI tools and browser extensions. None of that is wrong in itself. The questions cover the places where copies pile up and are easy to forget:

- Searchable CV databases and public PDFs: anyone who can search or follow the link can read it, and public files can end up in search engines.

- What’s on the CV: the less personal detail it carries, the less any leak or over-share matters.

- Trackers, CV builders and scanners with accounts: each one is another copy to keep track of and, eventually, delete.

- Browser extensions: an extension that can read every website sees more than the job ads it was installed for.

- AI tools: some services may use conversations to improve their models unless you change a setting.

- Agencies, visibility and email: who forwards your CV, who can see that you’re looking, and which mailbox the replies land in.

## Your rights in the EU

Under the GDPR you can ask any company that holds your CV which data it has about you (Article 15, right of access) and have it deleted when there’s no longer a reason to keep it (Article 17, right to erasure). Most services have a delete-account option or a privacy contact for this; a short email naming the article is enough.

## Where HireWire fits

HireWire is a job feed and application tracker that keeps your profile, CV text and pipeline in your browser, with no account. That takes care of one question above: your tracker. It doesn’t change your CV, your job-board settings or what you paste elsewhere. See exactly what HireWire stores and sends (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html), or the checklist for judging any job tracker (https://hirewire.fyi/are-free-job-trackers-safe.html). If you need a CV without handing it to another service, the free CV builder (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html) runs entirely in your browser: no account, no upload, PDF download.

## FAQ

**Q: Are my answers sent anywhere?**

No. The score is worked out by JavaScript in this page. Nothing is uploaded, stored or logged, and HireWire’s guide and tool pages load no analytics. Like every HireWire page, it loads its fonts from Google Fonts.

**Q: Is a high score bad?**

It means your CV is in many places, some of them public. That’s common during an active search and easy to reduce: work through the fixes from the top, and repeat the check after your search ends.

**Q: Does the check judge specific job boards or AI tools?**

No. Services and their settings change too often for that. The questions ask about what you did and what you can check yourself, such as a visibility setting or an extension’s permissions.

**Q: How do I get my CV deleted from a site?**

Look for “delete account” in its settings first. If there isn’t one, write to its privacy contact asking for erasure under Article 17 GDPR, and ask under Article 15 which data they hold if you’re unsure what’s there.

**Q: Is there a German version?**

Yes: Lebenslauf-Datenschutz-Check (https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-datenschutz-check.html), with the same questions and scoring.
