URL: https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html
Title: Free ATS CV Builder, No Sign-Up: Templates + PDF Download | HireWire

Free tool · CV builder

# Free ATS CV builder, no sign-up

Fill in the form, pick a template, download a PDF. No account, no paywall when you download, no watermark. Your CV is written and stored only in this browser: nothing is uploaded to HireWire or anyone else.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-21

## How it works

- Fill in the form. Start empty or press More → Load example to see a finished CV. The preview updates as you type.

- Pick a template. Classic, Modern and Compact are single-column CVs that applicant tracking systems (ATS) read reliably. German Lebenslauf is the tabular layout German employers expect.

- Download the PDF. “Download PDF” opens your browser’s print dialog; choose Save as PDF. The PDF contains real, selectable text, not an image.

- Match it to jobs (optional). “Score it against live jobs” opens HireWire with your CV loaded, so it can pick out your skills and rank postings by fit.

## The templates

| Template | Best for | Layout |

| Classic | Most applications, traditional industries | Serif type, centred name, one column |

| Modern | Tech, product, design, start-ups | Sans-serif, a single accent colour, one column |

| Compact | Fitting a lot onto one page | Smaller type and tighter spacing, one column |

| German Lebenslauf | Applications in Germany, Austria and Switzerland | Dates on the left, details on the right, optional photo, place, date and signature line |

You can switch templates at any time without retyping anything, and set the CV language (English or German headings and dates) and the paper size (A4 or US Letter) separately.

## Why these templates are ATS-friendly

An applicant tracking system turns your PDF back into text before anyone reads it. Layouts that look clever to a person can come out scrambled. The three ATS templates follow the rules that keep the text clean:

- one column, read top to bottom, with no text boxes, tables or sidebars;

- standard section names (Summary, Experience, Education, Skills, Languages) that parsers recognise;

- contact details in the body of the page, not in a header or footer;

- no icons, skill bars or photos, and common fonts (Georgia or Arial and their equivalents);

- real text in the PDF, so a parser or a recruiter can search and copy it.

No tool can promise how a particular employer’s system scores you; the content still has to match the job. For that part, see the Jobscan alternative (https://hirewire.fyi/jobscan-alternative.html) page or score your CV against a posting in HireWire.

## Your CV stays in your browser

The builder is a single page of JavaScript. It makes no network requests while you write, loads no analytics, and the PDF is produced by your own browser. With Remember in this browser switched on (the default), the CV is kept in this browser’s local storage so it is still there next time; switch it off and it is deleted from storage straight away. To move it to another device, use More → Save as file and open the file there. More on how HireWire handles data on the privacy page (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html).

## From CV to job matches

A CV on its own does not find you a job. “Score it against live jobs” hands your CV to the HireWire app on this same site, still inside your browser: it reads your skills out of it, asks for the role and place you want, and ranks postings from 55 job feeds by fit. From there you can track applications, run an AI fit score on any posting (three free), or, with Pass Plus, have a tailored CV written for a specific job.

## FAQ

**Q: Is this an ATS CV builder?**

Yes, in the sense that matters: Classic, Modern and Compact are single-column layouts with standard section names, contact details in the page body, no icons or skill bars, and real text in the PDF, which applicant tracking systems read reliably. No tool can promise how a specific employer’s system will score you; the wording still has to match the job.

**Q: Is this CV builder really free?**

Yes. Building, editing and downloading your CV as a PDF is free, with no watermark and no sign-up. HireWire earns money from optional AI passes inside the job app, never from the CV builder.

**Q: Can I download my CV without signing up?**

Yes. There is no account at all. “Download PDF” uses your browser’s print dialog: choose Save as PDF as the destination, and turn off headers and footers for a clean page.

**Q: Where is my CV stored?**

Only in your browser’s local storage on this device, and only while Remember in this browser is on. Nothing is sent to HireWire. Clearing your browser data or pressing More → Clear everything deletes it.

**Q: Should I put a photo on my CV?**

For the UK, the US and Ireland, no: leave it out. In Germany a photo is common but not required, so the photo field appears only on the German Lebenslauf template.

**Q: Can I get a Word (.docx) file?**

Not from the builder; it produces a PDF, which most employers and portals prefer. If a portal asks for Word, the AI tools inside HireWire (Pass Plus) export DOCX for tailored CVs.

**Q: How long should my CV be?**

One page for up to about five years of experience, two pages beyond that. The preview shows the page count and marks where each page breaks.

**Q: Is there a German version?**

Yes: Lebenslauf-Vorlage kostenlos (https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-vorlage.html), the same builder with German labels and the tabular Lebenslauf selected.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

People actively job hunting who picked a free, local-first tool. The 55 job feeds lean towards tech, product and remote roles, including German and EU employers.

None on the slot. A plain link, no redirect, no click logging, no referrer.

Price

## What you get

HireWire is a free job feed and application tracker at hirewire.fyi (https://hirewire.fyi/). It pulls 55 public job feeds into one list, scores postings against the user’s own profile and tracks applications, with everything kept in the user’s browser. Sponsors help keep the core free.

Your product

One line about why it matters to someone in a job search.

Your button text

## “No tracking” is the point

Your link opens in a new tab as a plain link with rel="sponsored noopener noreferrer". There’s no redirect through HireWire and no click event, so we can’t see who clicks. Because of noreferrer, the browser doesn’t tell your site the visitor came from hirewire.fyi either, so you can’t see who our users are. For a privacy brand that is the pitch: you reach people who care about tracking, in a place that keeps its promise, and nobody gets profiled along the way.

The same way you’d measure a podcast read or a print ad:

- A URL only HireWire users see, such as yourbrand.com/hirewire, counted in your own analytics.

- A dedicated landing page you host, so measurement stays on your side end to end.

- From us: the exact dates your card ran, a screenshot of it live, and the total number of app page loads during your run from our anonymous, cookieless counts. Never per person, and never clicks.

Every slot is hand-sold and hand-picked. Good fits are products that respect their users’ privacy and help with a job search or a working life: private email, VPNs, password managers, private search and browsers, and career tools that don’t sell data. We say no to data brokers, behavioural ad networks, “guaranteed job” offers and recruiting spam.

## What HireWire tracks itself

We’d rather you hear it from us. The app page counts anonymous feature use with PostHog: named events only, no autocapture, no session recording, no cookies, nothing at all unless the visitor opts in (and never under Do Not Track), and never sponsor clicks. With a code or URL that only HireWire users get: you count redemptions or visits on your side. We add the dates your card ran and the total app page loads in that period.

Title: What Is the Best Free Browser-Based Job Application Tracker? (2026)

Buyer’s guide

# What is the best free browser-based job application tracker?

It depends on whether you want to find jobs, log them, or have AI write for you. Here are the criteria, and where each option lands.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

## Short answer

- Best for finding and tracking with no account: HireWire. It ranks 55 live job feeds against your profile and tracks the jobs you save, all inside your browser. It has no manual entry.

- Best for manual tracking with no account: JobsTracker (jobstracker.org). You add any application, it reads pasted recruiter emails, and it offers optional encryption.

- Best cloud suite with AI writing: Huntr or Teal. Both need an account. Huntr’s free plan tracks up to 100 jobs. Teal’s free plan has unlimited tracking.

- Most flexible: a spreadsheet, if you don’t mind doing all the work yourself.

Disclosure: this page is published by HireWire. We have tried to state where other tools are better, and we mark anything we couldn’t verify.

## Criteria that actually matter

- Real cost. Is tracking free without a limit, or is there a cap that forces an upgrade mid-search?

- Account and data location. Does your search history sit on a vendor’s server, or only on your device?

- Getting jobs in. Do you type every role, clip it from a site, or does the tool find postings for you?

- Exit. Can you export everything in an open format (JSON or CSV) whenever you want?

- Follow-through. Does it tell you what has gone quiet and what to do next?

- Durability. Browser-only tools can lose data when site storage is cleared. Is there a one-step backup?

## How the options compare

| | HireWire | JobsTracker (.org) | Huntr | Teal | Spreadsheet |

| Free tracking | Unlimited | Unlimited | Up to 100 jobs | Unlimited | Unlimited |

| Paid tier | Optional one-time AI passes: €9 / 7 days, €19 / 30 days, Pass Plus €29 / 30 days | None | $40/mo | Teal+ $13/week or $29 per 30 days | — |

| Account | No | No | Yes | Yes | Depends on the app |

| Data location | Your browser | Your browser | Vendor cloud | Vendor cloud | Your file or your cloud drive |

| Finds jobs | 55 feeds, ranked | No | Clipper (you find them) | Not verified for the free tracker | No |

| Manual entry | No | Yes | Yes | Not verified (advertises bookmarking jobs) | Yes |

| AI writing | With Pass Plus or your own key | No | Yes | Yes | No |

| Open export | JSON, CSV, MD | JSON | Not verified | Not verified | Native |

Checked 2026-10-14 against each product’s own pricing, privacy or app pages. Details: HireWire vs JobsTracker (https://hirewire.fyi/hirewire-vs-jobstracker.html), HireWire vs Huntr (https://hirewire.fyi/hirewire-vs-huntr.html).

## Where HireWire fits, honestly

HireWire is strongest if your search is mainly remote or tech roles. Its feeds are remote boards (Remotive, RemoteOK, We Work Remotely and others) and career pages of companies such as Stripe, OpenAI, Linear and Vercel, plus German employers such as N26, Celonis, Trade Republic and Delivery Hero. You can widen coverage with a free Adzuna key. It scores each posting by your skills, your salary floor in your own currency, freshness and blocked keywords. It also drafts follow-ups when an application goes quiet for 14 days.

It is weakest if most of your applications come from outside its feeds: LinkedIn, local job sites or recruiter emails. HireWire can only save postings from its feeds. Pair it with a spreadsheet, or choose a manual tracker.

## A simple way to choose

- You want something to surface roles each morning: HireWire.

- You apply everywhere and only need a log: JobsTracker or a spreadsheet.

- You want résumé rewriting and autofill and don’t mind an account: Huntr or Teal.

- Your search is confidential: pick a no-account tool, then read what to check before trusting a free tracker (https://hirewire.fyi/are-free-job-trackers-safe.html).

## FAQ

**Q: What is the best free browser-based job application tracker?**

For finding and tracking jobs with no account, HireWire. It ranks 55 public job feeds against your profile and keeps everything in your browser. For logging applications by hand with no account, JobsTracker (jobstracker.org). For a cloud suite with AI résumé tools, Huntr or Teal.

**Q: Is there a job tracker that doesn’t need an account?**

Yes. HireWire and JobsTracker (jobstracker.org) both run entirely in your browser with no sign-up. A local spreadsheet also needs none.

**Q: Are browser-based job trackers safe from data loss?**

Only if you back up. Browser storage is deleted when you clear site data, and Safari can delete it after 7 days without a visit. Use the tool’s export regularly. HireWire shows a reminder when your backup is out of date.

Title: Are Free Job Trackers Safe? A 10-Point Privacy Checklist for Job Seekers

Guide

# Are free job trackers safe?

Usually safe enough, if you know what you’re handing over. A job search is a detailed record of your career, salary expectations and contacts. Here is how to judge any free tracker in ten minutes.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-14

## What a job tracker can know about you

Over a few months, a tracker builds up your CV, every company you applied to, salary figures, interview notes, recruiter names and emails, and sometimes your inbox. For someone searching while still employed, that is sensitive. A “free” product still pays its costs somehow, usually through a paid upgrade, ads, or (less often) data. None of that is automatically bad, but you should know which one applies.

## Three architectures, three risk profiles

| Type | Where your data is | Main risk |

| Cloud tracker with account | Vendor servers and their providers | Breach, policy changes, data kept after you leave, broad email permissions |

| Browser extension | Varies: local, cloud or both | Permission to read the pages you visit. Updates can change behaviour |

| Local-first web app (e.g. HireWire, jobstracker.org) | Your browser’s storage | Data loss when site data is cleared. Third-party scripts on the page |

## The 10-point checklist

- Is an account required? No account means there is no profile of you on a vendor’s server.

- Where is data stored? Look for a plain statement: “in your browser”, or a named cloud region and provider.

- Does it want your inbox? Full Gmail or Outlook access is the largest permission a tracker can ask for. Prefer tools that let you paste an email, or that request read-only, narrowly scoped access.

- Is your CV uploaded? If it is, find out whether it goes to an AI provider, and whether it is kept.

- What analytics run, and where? Look for session recording or autocapture (which can record what you type) as opposed to named, counted events.

- Ads and trackers. Ad networks set cookies. Check whether they run inside the app or only on marketing pages.

- Can you export everything? An open JSON or CSV export means you can leave at any time.

- Can you delete your data? For cloud tools, is there self-serve account deletion? For local tools, clearing site data does it.

- Free-tier limits. A cap (for example 100 jobs) can force an upgrade halfway through a search. Know it before you start.

- Backups. For local tools, is there one-click backup, and does it remind you to use it?

## Warning signs

- A privacy policy that doesn’t mention the tracker app at all, or no policy.

- “We may share data with partners” with no list of who.

- Inbox access required just to use the basic tracker.

- No export, or export only on a paid plan.

- Session-replay tools running inside the app where you type notes.

## How HireWire answers the checklist

HireWire answers to the same standard:

- No account. Data is kept in browser localStorage, mirrored to IndexedDB.

- No inbox access. The CV is pasted and processed in the page, and only extracted skill keywords are kept.

- Analytics: PostHog with autocapture and session recording off. It sends named feature events only and is skipped under Do Not Track.

- No ad networks. Sponsor slots are plain links with no click tracking.

- Full JSON backup, plus .md, .json and .csv exports. A reminder appears when your backup is out of date.

- Its weak spot is the local-first one: if you clear site data without a backup, the data is gone.

The full detail is on the privacy page (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html).

## FAQ

**Q: Are free job trackers safe?**

Most reputable ones are reasonably safe, but “free” covers very different set-ups. Check whether an account is required, where data is stored, whether it wants inbox access, what analytics and ads run in the app, and whether you can export and delete your data.

**Q: Is it safe to connect my Gmail to a job tracker?**

It can be, but it is the broadest permission a tracker can ask for. Prefer tools that work from pasted emails, or that ask only for read-only, narrowly scoped access. Review connected apps in your Google account settings and remove ones you no longer use.

**Q: Are local, browser-only trackers safer?**

For privacy, generally yes, because there is no server copy to leak. The trade-off is durability. Clearing browser data or Safari’s 7-day rule can erase it, so keep backups.

## Related

- Privacy, in plain language (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html)

- Best free browser-based job tracker (https://hirewire.fyi/best-browser-job-tracker.html)

- HireWire vs Huntr (https://hirewire.fyi/hirewire-vs-huntr.html)

Title: Job Tracker vs Spreadsheet: When a Local App Wins (and When It Doesn’t)

Use case

# Job tracker vs spreadsheet

A spreadsheet is the most flexible tracker there is. It just doesn’t do anything on its own. Here is when a local app earns its place, and when it doesn’t.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-14

## Short answer

- Use a spreadsheet if most of your roles come from referrals, recruiters or sites a tracker can’t read, or if you want custom columns and formulas.

- Use a local app like HireWire if you want roles to come to you, ranked, with stage dates, follow-up flags and pay filtering handled for you, still with no account.

- Use both if you do both. Many active searches do.

## Side-by-side

| | HireWire (local app) | Spreadsheet |

| Setup | Open the page, add skills and a salary floor | Design columns, statuses and validation yourself |

| Getting roles in | 55 public feeds refresh hourly, ranked by match | Copy and paste every role |

| Roles from anywhere | No. Wire postings only | Yes |

| Salary filtering | Floor in your currency, converted automatically (rough static rates) | Manual, or your own formulas |

| Stage history | Date stamped automatically for every stage | Only if you add a column per stage |

| Follow-ups | Flags 14 days of silence and drafts the email | Conditional formatting, if you build it |

| Funnel metrics | Built in: conversion, days per stage, source yield | Pivot tables |

| Custom fields | Notes, contacts, next date, offer figures | Unlimited |

| Sharing with a coach or partner | Export .csv, .md or .json | Native (for cloud spreadsheets) |

| Privacy | Browser storage only, no account | A local file is private. A cloud sheet lives in your Google or Microsoft account |

| Durability | Clearing site data wipes it, so keep a JSON backup | Very durable, especially in cloud drives |

| Multi-device | Via backup file | Native, for cloud spreadsheets |

## Where spreadsheets win

Total flexibility. You can add a column for visa sponsorship, commute time or the name of the friend who referred you. You can share a link with a career coach. Nothing breaks if you apply through a channel no tool supports. And a spreadsheet will still open in ten years.

## Where a local app wins

The parts of a search that are tedious by hand. Checking the same boards every morning, working out whether a €75,000 role clears a $90k floor, remembering which application went quiet two weeks ago, and counting how many applications turned into screens. HireWire does these automatically, and it does it without an account, so there’s no cloud trade-off.

## A combined set-up that works

- Use HireWire as your discovery and pipeline for roles on the wire. Pin, stage and follow up there.

- Keep a spreadsheet for everything else: referrals, recruiter emails, local roles. The recruiter posts guide (https://hirewire.fyi/guides/bulk-import-recruiter-job-posts.html) gives a column layout.

- Once a week, export HireWire’s pipeline as CSV (open the console with ` or Ctrl+K and type export csv pipeline) if you want one combined view. Columns: title, company, source, remote, location, posted, salary, score, status, note, url.

- Back up HireWire (Backup everything) whenever you update the spreadsheet.

## FAQ

**Q: Is a spreadsheet good enough to track job applications?**

Yes, for many people. It is flexible and durable. A tracker app adds automatic stage dates, follow-up reminders, metrics and, in HireWire’s case, a ranked feed of new roles.

**Q: Can I export HireWire to Google Sheets or Excel?**

Yes. Open the console (press ` or Ctrl+K) and type export csv pipeline to download your pipeline as CSV. The CSV button in the sidebar exports the current scored shortlist. Then open or import the file in your spreadsheet.

**Q: Can I import a spreadsheet into HireWire?**

No. HireWire has no spreadsheet import, and it can only save postings that appear on its feeds.

Title: HireWire vs JobsTracker (jobstracker.org) — Two Local-First Job Trackers Compared

Comparison

# HireWire vs JobsTracker (jobstracker.org)

Two free trackers with the same privacy stance: no account, no cloud, data in your browser. They differ in what they do with that data.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-14

There are at least two products called “JobsTracker”. This page covers jobstracker.org, the local-first browser tracker. For the AI-powered one launched on Product Hunt at jobstracker.app, see HireWire vs JobsTracker (jobstracker.app) (https://hirewire.fyi/hirewire-vs-jobstracker-app.html).

## Verdict

- Choose JobsTracker if you apply through many channels and want to log each application by hand, score your résumé against a pasted job description, and let it read pasted recruiter emails to update status. It also offers optional passphrase encryption.

- Choose HireWire if you also want to find roles. It pulls 55 public job feeds, ranks them against your skills and salary floor, and tracks the ones you save through a six-stage pipeline with follow-up drafts, insights and agent briefs.

- On privacy they are close. Both keep data in the browser with no account. HireWire’s app page has cookieless usage analytics (off under Do Not Track). JobsTracker’s app page has none, though its marketing pages use Google Analytics.

## Side-by-side

| | HireWire | JobsTracker (jobstracker.org) |

| Price | Free | Free (“no account, no subscription, no paywall”) |

| Account | None | None |

| Where data lives | localStorage, mirrored to IndexedDB | localStorage |

| Encryption at rest | No | Optional passphrase (exports are unencrypted) |

| Finds jobs for you | Yes: 55 public feeds, plus optional Adzuna and Jooble keys | No job feed advertised. You add applications yourself |

| Add an application by hand | No. Only postings from the wire can be saved | Yes |

| Fit / match scoring | Every posting scored against skills, salary floor (currency-converted), freshness, remote and blocked keywords | Résumé-to-job-description fit badge with matched and missing keywords |

| Salary filter | Yes: floor in 12 currencies | No salary field in the app’s data model |

| Résumé / CV handling | Paste text, extract skills locally. The text isn’t stored | Upload .txt or .pdf, read locally and stored in the browser |

| Recruiter email parsing | No | Yes: paste an email and it sets Interviewing, Offer or Closed, and flags emails that need a reply |

| Pipeline stages | Saved, applied, screen, interview, offer, archived | Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Respond, Closed, Ghosted |

| Follow-ups | Flags jobs 14 days quiet and drafts a follow-up email. Calendar (.ics) export | “Needs response” inbox for pasted emails |

| Contacts / referrals | Per-job contacts plus a People ledger with 10-day nudges | Not verified |

| Analytics / insights | Funnel conversion, days per stage, source yield, offer comparison, weekly digest | Dashboard: totals, interviews, offers, response rate |

| AI-agent export | Markdown, JSON or CSV brief for Claude Code, Cursor or Codex | No (status detection runs locally, “no AI service”) |

| Backup / restore | One JSON file. Restore by button or drag and drop | JSON export and import |

| Tracking on the app page | PostHog, cookieless, named feature events only, off under Do Not Track | None, per its privacy policy. Google Analytics on marketing pages; AdSense planned |

| Ads | Hand-sold sponsor slots with no click tracking | Advertisement slot on its site; AdSense “planned” |

| Mobile app or sync | No | Not verified (Gmail sync described as planned) |

Sources: jobstracker.org home page, its privacy page (last updated 2026-06-17) and the public app code, checked 2026-10-14. HireWire: the app’s source at hirewire.fyi.

## Where JobsTracker is stronger

It is built for the applications you find yourself. You can add any role from any source, paste in a recruiter’s reply and have the status set for you, and see at a glance which threads need an answer. If an encrypted local store matters to you, for example on a shared computer, JobsTracker has it and HireWire doesn’t.

## Where HireWire is stronger

HireWire covers discovery as well as tracking. It ranks a few hundred live postings by your criteria every hour, hides blocked locations, filters by a salary floor across currencies, and keeps dates per stage so it can show conversion and time-to-screen. For developers, the agent brief turns the shortlist into a task for a coding agent.

## Using both

They don’t conflict. Some people find and rank roles in HireWire and log off-board applications in a manual tracker. If you want to consolidate, see moving from JobsTracker to HireWire (https://hirewire.fyi/guides/migrate-from-jobstracker.html). It is a manual path, and the guide explains why.

## FAQ

**Q: Is JobsTracker the same as HireWire?**

No. They are separate, unrelated products. Both are free browser-based trackers with no account, but JobsTracker is a manual tracker with résumé fit and email status detection, while HireWire is a job feed aggregator with a tracker built in.

**Q: Which one is more private?**

Both keep your data in the browser with no server copy. JobsTracker’s app page has no analytics and offers passphrase encryption. HireWire’s app page sends cookieless feature-usage events unless Do Not Track is on. Neither uploads your CV.

**Q: Can I move my JobsTracker data into HireWire?**

Not with one click. HireWire has no import for other trackers’ files. The migration guide (https://hirewire.fyi/guides/migrate-from-jobstracker.html) covers the manual options.

- Move from JobsTracker to HireWire (https://hirewire.fyi/guides/migrate-from-jobstracker.html)

Title: HireWire vs JobsTracker (jobstracker.app) — AI Job Tracker vs Local-First Tracker

Comparison

# HireWire vs JobsTracker (jobstracker.app)

Not to be confused with jobstracker.org. This JobsTracker is described as an AI-powered tracker, and when we checked it, its site was offline.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-14

Looking for the local-first browser tracker at jobstracker.org? See HireWire vs JobsTracker (jobstracker.org) (https://hirewire.fyi/hirewire-vs-jobstracker.html).

## What we could verify

- JobsTracker’s Product Hunt listing describes it as “an AI-powered job applications tracker” that “scrapes job postings, extracts key details with AI, and streamlines your path to your next role”. It is listed as Free and launched in 2026. The listing links to jobstracker.app.

- On 2026-10-14, jobstracker.app returned an HTTP 402 page reading “JobsTracker is currently unavailable”. The page identifies it as an app built on the Base44 platform.

Because the product wasn’t reachable, we couldn’t check its account requirements, storage, pricing or privacy policy. We have not guessed at them.

## Side-by-side

| | HireWire | JobsTracker (jobstracker.app) |

| Availability (2026-10-14) | Live at hirewire.fyi | Site showed “currently unavailable” |

| Price | Free | Listed as Free on Product Hunt |

| Account required | No | Not verified |

| Where data is stored | Your browser (localStorage + IndexedDB) | Not verified. Built on a hosted app platform (Base44) |

| Uses AI | Optional AI fit score (Google Gemini) per posting, only when you press it. Also exports a brief for your own agent | Yes: AI extraction of posting details, per its listing |

| How jobs get in | 55 public feeds, plus optional Adzuna and Jooble keys | Scrapes job postings, per its listing |

| Match scoring | Skills, salary floor, freshness, remote, blocked keywords | Not verified |

| Backup / export | Full JSON backup. Exports in .md, .json and .csv | Not verified |

| Privacy policy | Plain-language page (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html) | Not verified |

## The real trade-off: AI extraction vs local-only

An AI tracker that scrapes postings for you saves typing. To do that, the posting (and often your account data) passes through the vendor’s servers and an AI model provider. A local-first tool like HireWire doesn’t send your profile or pipeline anywhere. The trade-off is that it only tracks postings from its feeds and has no manual entry.

Before you put a job search into any hosted tracker, ask three questions. Can I export everything? Is an account required, and can I delete it? Which third parties process what I paste in? Our guide to free job tracker safety (https://hirewire.fyi/are-free-job-trackers-safe.html) covers what to check.

## If JobsTracker (jobstracker.app) was your tracker

If the app is offline and you can still reach an export, save it as CSV or JSON now. HireWire can’t import another tracker’s file directly. A spreadsheet is the safest home for that history. See job tracker vs spreadsheet (https://hirewire.fyi/job-tracker-vs-spreadsheet.html).

## FAQ

**Q: Is jobstracker.app the same as jobstracker.org?**

They appear to be different products. jobstracker.org is a local-first browser tracker. jobstracker.app is listed on Product Hunt as an AI-powered tracker. We found no link between them.

**Q: Is JobsTracker (jobstracker.app) still available?**

When we checked on 2026-10-14, the site showed “currently unavailable”. Check the site yourself for its current status.

Title: HireWire vs Huntr — A Privacy-Focused, No-Account Huntr Alternative

Comparison

# HireWire vs Huntr

Huntr is a polished cloud platform with AI résumé tools. HireWire is a free, no-account, browser-only alternative for people who would rather their job search not live on someone else’s server.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

## Verdict

- Huntr is the better fit if you want an all-in-one cloud suite: a Chrome job clipper that saves jobs from any site, application autofill, AI résumé tailoring and cover letters, document storage, a mobile app and sync across devices. The free plan tracks up to 100 jobs. Pro is $40/month.

- HireWire is the better fit if privacy and price come first. There is no account, nothing is stored on a server, and the core app is free; only the optional AI fit score is paid, as a one-time pass rather than a subscription. It also finds jobs for you from 55 public feeds and scores them. It has no clipper and no autofill. AI cover letters and tailored CV drafts come with the optional Pass Plus (€29 for 30 days, one-time), and encrypted sync with any pass.

## Side-by-side

| | HireWire | Huntr |

| Price | Free core. Optional AI fit score: 3 free, then €9 for 7 days or €19 for 30 days (one-time) | Free plan. Pro $40/month, $90 per 3 months or $160 per 6 months |

| Tracking limit | None set (limited only by browser storage) | Free: up to 100 jobs. Pro: unlimited |

| Account | None | Sign-up required |

| Where your data lives | Your browser (localStorage + IndexedDB) | Huntr’s cloud. Its policy lists third parties for authentication, payments (Stripe), site analytics, AI content creation, data storage, hosting, email and support |

| Cookies | None | Uses cookies “to collect information about you and your activity” |

| Sells data | No data to sell. Analytics counts feature use only | Says it “will never sell your personal data” |

| Finds jobs for you | Yes: 55 public feeds, ranked by match score | You save jobs from job sites with the Chrome clipper |

| Save a job from any website | No. Only postings on the wire | Yes: Chrome job clipper |

| Match scoring | Skills, salary floor (12 currencies), freshness, remote, blocked keywords | Résumé-to-job matching (basic on Free, advanced on Pro) |

| AI résumé and cover letters | Pass Plus (€29 / 30 days, one-time) or your own Anthropic key: cover letter, tailored CV draft, interview prep, negotiation script | Yes. Unlimited on Pro, a few credits on Free |

| Application autofill | No | Yes (Chrome extension) |

| Contacts | Per-job contacts and a People ledger | Contact tracker (unlimited on Free) |

| Metrics | Funnel conversion, days per stage, source yield, offer comparison | Basic job insights on Free. Advanced metrics on Pro |

| Document storage | No | Up to 100 uploads on Free, unlimited on Pro |

| Mobile / multi-device | Works in a mobile browser. Installable web app. End-to-end encrypted sync with any pass, or a free JSON backup | Mobile app and cloud sync |

| Export your data | Full JSON backup, plus .md, .json and .csv exports | Not verified |

Huntr facts are from huntr.co/pricing and huntr.co/privacy, checked 2026-10-14. Prices are in USD and may change.

## Why someone looks for a Huntr alternative

The two common reasons are cost and data. Huntr Pro costs $40 a month. The free plan caps tracking at 100 jobs, which an active search can reach in a few weeks. And a cloud tracker holds a detailed record of your search: who you applied to, your notes, your résumé. That record sits under an account with a list of service providers. For many people that’s fine. For people searching while still employed, or who simply don’t want that record held anywhere, a local tool is the cleaner option.

## What you give up by switching to HireWire

Be clear-eyed about the gaps. HireWire can’t clip a job from LinkedIn or a company site. It only tracks postings that appear on its feeds, which lean towards remote and tech roles. Its free CV builder (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html) is basic (four templates, PDF, no AI tailoring); AI writing needs Pass Plus or your own key. If you rely on the clipper or autofill daily, Huntr will save you more time.

## What you gain

You get a tracker with no sign-up, no cap and no subscription, where everything you type stays on your device. You also get job discovery built in: an hourly-refreshed, ranked list from 55 feeds, filtered by your salary floor and blocked locations, with a follow-up draft when an application goes quiet.

## FAQ

**Q: Is HireWire a free alternative to Huntr?**

Yes, for job tracking and discovery. HireWire is free with no account and no job limit. It doesn’t replace Huntr’s résumé builder, Chrome clipper or autofill.

**Q: Does Huntr require an account?**

Yes. Huntr’s free and Pro plans both start with a sign-up, and your data is stored in Huntr’s cloud.

**Q: How much is Huntr Pro?**

Per huntr.co/pricing (checked 2026-10-14): $40 billed monthly, $90 every 3 months, or $160 every 6 months.

**Q: Can I import my Huntr data into HireWire?**

No. HireWire has no importer for other trackers. Keep your Huntr history in a spreadsheet and start fresh in HireWire for new roles.

# A free Huntr alternative with no job limit

Huntr’s free plan tracks up to 100 jobs; after that it’s Huntr Pro at $40 a month. If you mainly need tracking, here is a free option with no cap, and an honest list of what you’d miss.

# A Teal job tracker alternative that keeps your job search on your device

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

- Choose Teal if résumé writing is the main job: AI résumé builder, templates, cover letters, keyword matching, and a Chrome extension that bookmarks jobs from many job boards. The tracker is free and unlimited. Teal+ unlocks unlimited AI and analysis.

- Choose HireWire if you want jobs to come to you and your search to stay private. It ranks postings from 55 public feeds against your skills and salary floor, flags ghost jobs, drafts follow-ups and needs no account. Its CV builder (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html) is free but basic.

- Many people can use both: Teal for the CV, HireWire for discovery and a private pipeline.

## Why people look for a Teal job tracker alternative

Usually for one of three reasons. Some don’t want another account holding a detailed record of their job search, especially while still employed. Some find that the free AI credits run out fast and Teal+ is billed every week, month or quarter until they cancel. And some don’t need a résumé builder at all; they need help finding the right postings and keeping up with follow-ups.

## What you give up with HireWire

Be clear-eyed. HireWire’s CV builder (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html) is deliberately basic (four templates, PDF, no AI suggestions), and its AI writing is a paid add-on (or needs your own key) rather than free credits. Its feeds lean towards remote and tech roles, so it won’t show every local job. Until the browser extension is published, you can only track postings that came through its feeds. If you want one tool that writes your CV and tracks everything you bookmark, Teal is the better fit.

- No account, no cloud copy. Your profile, pipeline, notes and contacts stay in your browser. See exactly what leaves the page (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html).

- Jobs come to you. An hourly-refreshed list from 55 feeds, sorted by fit with your skills, salary floor and blocked keywords.

- Fewer wasted applications. A ghost-job risk (https://hirewire.fyi/ghost-job-checker.html) on every posting and a salary reality check (https://hirewire.fyi/salary-checker.html).

- Pay once, if at all. The AI fit score is optional: 3 free, then a 7- or 30-day pass that doesn’t renew.

Alternative

# A Jobscan alternative without the subscription

Jobscan is built around résumé scanning for applicant-tracking systems. HireWire comes at it from the other side: find the right postings first, then score your CV against the ones worth applying to, with no account and no recurring bill.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-15

- Choose Jobscan if you want an ATS-style résumé scan with match rates, unlimited scans and AI optimisation, LinkedIn optimisation and auto-apply credits, and you’re fine with a subscription and an account.

- Choose HireWire if you want a fit score with concrete fixes for the few jobs you really apply to, a free job feed and tracker, and your search kept in your browser. It does not simulate an ATS or check CV formatting.

## Is a one-time pass better than a subscription?

It depends on how you search. Scanning a résumé against dozens of postings a week favours unlimited scans. If you apply to a handful of carefully chosen roles, paying once for 7 or 30 days, with no renewal to remember to cancel, is simpler. HireWire’s pass is per browser and needs no account: you get a pass ID to restore it on another device.

## What HireWire doesn’t do

HireWire doesn’t parse your CV file, check its layout or predict how a particular applicant-tracking system will read it. Its score is an AI judgement of fit and wording, and its rewrites only re-phrase what your CV already says (numbers it can’t find become placeholders for you to fill). If your worry is formatting, see our ATS tips for CVs (https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-ats-tipps.html) (in German) or use a dedicated scanner.

## What you get for free

- A ranked feed of postings from 55 public sources, refreshed hourly.

- A private pipeline with notes, contacts, follow-up reminders and email drafts.

- A free keyword gap check of any pasted posting against your profile skills (Tailor tab).

- A ghost-job risk (https://hirewire.fyi/ghost-job-checker.html) and a salary reality check (https://hirewire.fyi/salary-checker.html).

**Q: Is there a free Jobscan alternative?**

For tracking and finding jobs, HireWire is free with no account. Its AI fit score gives 3 free scores, then costs a one-time pass (€9 for 7 days, €19 for 30 days) or is free with your own Anthropic API key.

**Q: How much does Jobscan cost?**

Per Jobscan’s pricing page on 15 Oct 2026: $49.95 billed monthly, or $89.95 every 3 months after a 7-day free trial. The free plan includes 5 résumé scans a month.

**Q: Does HireWire check if my CV is ATS-friendly?**

No. It rates how well your CV fits a specific posting and suggests better wording. It doesn’t analyse your file’s formatting. For the format, its free ATS CV builder (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html) produces single-column PDFs with real text and standard headings.

**Q: Is my CV stored when I use the AI fit score?**

No. It is sent only when you press Score, used for that one request and not stored or logged by HireWire. The full data flow is on the privacy page (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html#ai-fit-score).

URL: https://hirewire.fyi/guides/filter-jobs-by-minimum-pay.html
Title: How to Filter Jobs by Minimum Salary (Across Currencies) — HireWire Guide

Guide

# How to filter jobs by minimum pay

Set one number, your salary floor, and HireWire filters and scores every posting against it, even when the posting is in a different currency. Here is exactly how it decides.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-14

## Set your floor

- In Subscriber profile, pick the currency your floor is in: USD, EUR, GBP, INR, CAD, AUD, JPY, BRL, PLN, SGD, ZAR or MXN.

- Enter your salary floor (annual), for example 120k, 95000 or 1.2m.

- The ≥ Floor toggle in the wire toolbar switches on. Postings that don’t clear the floor disappear from the list.

In the console (press ` or Ctrl+K) the same thing is currency EUR and floor 85k. Type floor off to clear it. search rust --min=150k searches and sets the floor in one step. Note that it also updates your saved floor.

## How a posting is compared

HireWire compares the top of the posting’s pay range (its maximum, or its minimum if only one figure is given) with your floor. Both are converted to US dollars first.

- A role listed at $90k–$130k clears a $120k floor, because $130k ≥ $120k. The range shows the employer can reach your number. Whether they will is a negotiation.

- A role listed at up to $110k doesn’t clear it.

In the match score, clearing the floor adds 12 points. Falling below it subtracts 18. The posting’s “Matches” or “Watch” notes say which applied.

## Currency conversion

Conversion uses fixed, rough exchange rates built into the app (for example 1 EUR ≈ 1.09 USD and 1 GBP ≈ 1.27 USD), not live rates. That is fine for a floor, but don’t rely on it for borderline cases. If a role is within a few percent of your number, open it and check.

A posting’s currency comes from its source:

- Adzuna (with your key): the currency of the country you picked, such as GBP for the UK or EUR for Germany.

- Remotive, Jooble and HN “Who is hiring?”: read from the salary text. $, €, £ and ₹ (or USD, EUR, GBP, INR) are recognised. A bare “$” is treated as US dollars, so a CAD or AUD salary written with “$” is read as USD.

- RemoteOK: treated as USD.

European formats such as €75.000 – €95.000 are read correctly.

## Postings with no stated pay

Many sources don’t publish pay in their feeds. That includes most company career boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, SmartRecruiters, Personio, Recruitee) as well as Arbeitnow, Jobicy and We Work Remotely. These show PAY N/A.

- With ≥ Floor on, postings with no stated pay are hidden, because HireWire can’t confirm they clear your floor.

- With ≥ Floor off, they are shown and lose 3 points, with “pay unstated” in the Watch notes. Postings below your floor are shown too, minus 18.

Tip: if your list looks thin after setting a floor, switch ≥ Floor off. The floor still shapes the ranking, and good unpriced roles at companies you like stay visible.

## Hourly, daily and monthly rates

The floor is annual, and HireWire doesn’t convert pay periods. When it reads pay from text, it ignores figures below 15,000 to avoid picking up hourly rates and stray numbers. So $45/hour or €5,000/month counts as unstated. A large monthly figure written with a “k” (for example $20k/month) could be read as an annual $20k. For contract work, turn ≥ Floor off and judge the rate yourself.

## Related filters

- Blocked locations hide postings whose location matches, for example a country you can’t work from.

- Blocked keywords push postings down 28 points each.

- Remote limits the wire to remote roles. It is on by default.

## FAQ

**Q: Does HireWire hide jobs that don’t list a salary?**

Only while the ≥ Floor toggle is on and you have set a floor. Turn the toggle off to see them. They lose 3 points in the match score.

**Q: Which number in a salary range is compared to my floor?**

The top of the range (the maximum), converted to USD alongside your floor. If only one figure is listed, that figure is used.

**Q: Are exchange rates live?**

No. HireWire uses fixed approximate rates built into the app, so treat borderline results as approximate.

**Q: Can I set an hourly minimum?**

No. The floor is annual and pay periods aren’t converted. Hourly and most monthly figures are treated as unstated pay.

Title: Organise Recruiter Job Posts in Bulk: Spreadsheet Template & Tips

Guide

# How to bulk-organise job posts from recruiters

When recruiters send roles in batches (a list in an email, a PDF, a LinkedIn message), the fastest reliable system is a spreadsheet with one row per role. Then decide what, if anything, goes into a tracker.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-14

## Step 1: one row per role

Don’t paste a whole recruiter email into one cell. Split it so each role gets its own row, even if the same recruiter sent five roles. That makes sorting, de-duplicating and following up possible.

## Step 2: use these columns

| Column | What to put in it |

| Date received | The date the recruiter sent it (YYYY-MM-DD sorts correctly) |

| Company | The hiring company, not the agency. Write “Undisclosed (agency name)” if it isn’t named |

| Role | Job title as written |

| Location | City or country |

| Working arrangement | Remote / Hybrid / On-site |

| Salary min | A number only, e.g. 85000 |

| Salary max | A number only. Leave blank if not given |

| Currency | ISO code: USD, EUR, GBP… |

| Pay period | Year / Month / Day / Hour |

| Job URL | The posting link, if there is one |

| Recruiter | Name and agency |

| Source email subject | So you can find the original message again |

| Status | New / Interested / Applied / Screen / Interview / Offer / Declined / Closed |

| Next action | “Reply with CV”, “Ask for salary”, “Chase” |

| Follow-up date | When to act next |

Header row to copy:

Date received,Company,Role,Location,Working arrangement,Salary min,Salary max,Currency,Pay period,Job URL,Recruiter,Source email subject,Status,Next action,Follow-up date

Keeping Salary min, Salary max, Currency and Pay period in separate columns is what makes pay comparable later. A cell reading “£60–70k + bonus” can’t be sorted or filtered.

## Step 3: clean duplicates

Recruiters often send the same role, sometimes from different agencies. Before you act on anything:

- Sort by Company, then Role.

- Look for the same company and a near-identical title, for example “Senior Data Engineer” and “Data Engineer (Senior)”. Keep the row with the most information, and note the other recruiter in the Recruiter cell.

- Be careful with two agencies submitting you to the same role. It can disqualify you at some employers. Pick one and tell the other.

- In Google Sheets, Data → Data cleanup → Remove duplicates on Company + Role catches exact matches. Near-matches need a manual pass.

## Step 4: work the list

Sort by Follow-up date each morning. Add a filter view for Status = Interested or Applied. Use conditional formatting to highlight follow-up dates in the past.

## Step 5: only bulk-import into a tracker with a documented import

If you want these rows in a tracker app, check that the tool documents its import: the accepted file type, the required columns and how duplicates are handled. Importing into an undocumented format can quietly drop fields or overwrite existing records. Test with three rows first.

## Where HireWire fits

HireWire doesn’t have a spreadsheet or bulk import, and it can’t add roles by hand. It tracks postings that appear on its 55 public feeds. So for recruiter-sourced roles:

- Keep the spreadsheet above as the system of record for those roles.

- Search HireWire’s wire for the company. If the role is publicly posted on a board HireWire reads (for example a Greenhouse or Lever career page it covers), pin it there to get stage dates, follow-up flags and offer comparison.

- Use HireWire to find direct applications, so you aren’t relying only on recruiters.

## FAQ

**Q: What is the best way to track jobs that recruiters send me?**

A spreadsheet with one row per role and separate columns for company, role, location, working arrangement, salary min, salary max, currency, pay period, job URL, recruiter, source email subject, status, next action and follow-up date.

**Q: Can I bulk import recruiter roles into HireWire?**

No. HireWire has no import feature and no manual entry. It tracks postings from its public feeds. Keep recruiter roles in a spreadsheet.

**Q: How do I handle the same role sent by two recruiters?**

Keep one row, note both recruiters, and choose one agency to represent you. Being submitted twice can count against you.

**Q: Should salary be one column or several?**

Several: min, max, currency and pay period. That is the only way to sort and compare pay across roles reliably.

URL: https://hirewire.fyi/guides/migrate-from-jobstracker.html
Title: How to Move from JobsTracker to HireWire (Honest Migration Guide)

Guide

# How to move from JobsTracker to HireWire

The honest version. There is no one-click import, because the two apps store different things. Here are the options that work, from simplest to most technical.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-14

## Short answer

- Export your JobsTracker data first (Export gives a JSON backup).

- HireWire can’t import JobsTracker files. Its Restore only accepts HireWire backups, and it replaces your pipeline rather than merging.

- Recommended: keep your JobsTracker history as a CSV, and use HireWire for new roles from its feeds.

## What each app stores

| | JobsTracker export (jobstracker-backup-*.json) | HireWire backup (hirewire-backup-*.json) |

| Top level | version, exportedAt, jobs, resume | app: "HireWire", version: 2, exportedAt, profile, byok, board, savedSearches, starBank, people, settings |

| Per application | company, link, dateAdded, status, notes, jdText, emailText, fit data | job (title, company, location, remote, tags, url, postedAt, description, salary fields, source), status, note, at, contacts, log, comp, next, stageTs, appliedAt |

| Job title | No separate field | Required |

| Statuses | —, Applied, Interviewing, Offer, Respond, Closed, Ghosted | saved, applied, screen, interview, offer, archived |

Two things block a direct import. HireWire only restores files marked "app": "HireWire". And HireWire normally only tracks postings from its own feeds, so it has no form for entering an outside application.

## Option 1 (recommended): keep your history as a CSV

- In JobsTracker, click Export to download the JSON backup. Keep it, since it is your full record.

- Convert it to a CSV you can open in any spreadsheet. With Python installed, save this as jt2csv.py and run python3 jt2csv.py jobstracker-backup.json:

import csv, json, sys
data = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
with open("jobstracker-history.csv", "w", newline="") as f:
w = csv.writer(f)
w.writerow(["Date added", "Company", "Status", "Link", "Notes"])
for j in data.get("jobs", []):
w.writerow([j.get("dateAdded", ""), j.get("company", ""),
j.get("status", ""), j.get("link", ""), j.get("notes", "")])
print("wrote jobstracker-history.csv")

- Open the CSV in Google Sheets, Excel or Numbers. Add a Role column (JobsTracker doesn’t store titles separately) and the columns from our recruiter posts guide (https://hirewire.fyi/guides/bulk-import-recruiter-job-posts.html) if you want follow-up dates.

- Open HireWire (https://hirewire.fyi/), set your skills and salary floor, and pin new roles from the wire. If an active application of yours is on the wire (for example, it is posted on a Greenhouse or Lever board HireWire reads), pin it and set its stage. That carries it over properly.

## Option 2 (advanced): build a HireWire backup file

Technically, a HireWire backup is plain JSON. A file shaped like the one below will restore, and its entries will appear on My Board. This is not an official import, so be aware of the limits:

- Restore replaces your existing HireWire pipeline (and profile, people and saved searches, if those keys are present). Back up HireWire first, or merge entries into your existing backup’s board array.

- Imported entries have no feed source, so they won’t refresh and some features (full-description fetch, source yield) won’t do anything useful for them.

- Entries in applied or screen whose at date is more than 14 days old will show as “quiet” straight away.

{
"app": "HireWire",
"version": 2,
"board": [
{
"id": "import:jt:1",
"status": "applied",
"note": "Imported from JobsTracker",
"at": 1767225600000,
"job": {
"id": "import:jt:1", "source": "import",
"title": "Backend Engineer", "company": "Acme Corp",
"location": "—", "remote": "onsite", "tags": [],
"url": "https://example.com/job", "postedAt": 1767225600000,
"description": "", "salaryMin": null, "salaryMax": null,
"currency": "USD", "salaryText": ""
},
"contacts": [], "log": [], "next": null,
"stageTs": { "applied": 1767225600000 }, "appliedAt": 1767225600000
}
]
}

Dates are milliseconds since 1970 (UTC). Status mapping that fits most cases: Applied → applied, Interviewing → interview, Offer → offer, Respond → screen, Closed or Ghosted → archived, “—” → saved. A title and company are required on every job.

Restore the file with Restore… in the sidebar, or by dropping it on the page.

## Before you delete JobsTracker data

Keep the original JobsTracker JSON. It holds pasted job descriptions, recruiter emails and your résumé text, none of which HireWire can store per application. JobsTracker exports are unencrypted even if you used its passphrase feature, so store the file somewhere private.

## FAQ

**Q: Can HireWire import a JobsTracker backup?**

No. HireWire’s Restore only accepts HireWire backup files, and HireWire has no import for other trackers. Keep your history as a CSV, or build a HireWire-format backup as described above.

**Q: Will restoring a backup merge with my existing HireWire data?**

No. Restore replaces the pipeline, and the profile, people and saved searches if the file includes them. Back up first.

**Q: Does HireWire keep my résumé like JobsTracker does?**

No. HireWire extracts skill keywords from pasted CV text and stores only the keywords.

## Related

- HireWire vs JobsTracker (jobstracker.org) (https://hirewire.fyi/hirewire-vs-jobstracker.html)

- Job tracker vs spreadsheet (https://hirewire.fyi/job-tracker-vs-spreadsheet.html)

- Privacy, in plain language (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html)

- Guide & FAQ (https://hirewire.fyi/guide.html)

Title: English-Speaking Jobs in Germany: Free Job Aggregator, No Account | HireWire

Guide · Jobs in Germany

# English-speaking jobs in Germany: one free job list

If you work in English and want a job in Germany, or remote from Germany, the postings are scattered across company career pages and a few boards. HireWire puts them in one list, ranks them against your skills and keeps your search in your browser.

HireWire · last reviewed 2026-10-21

## Short answer

- HireWire is a free job aggregator: 55 public job feeds in one list, refreshed hourly while the tab is open, with no account.

- Germany is covered, not exclusive: career pages of German employers such as N26, Celonis, Trade Republic, Delivery Hero, DeepL, SIXT and Bosch, plus Arbeitnow, a board focused on jobs in Germany. Many other feeds are international and remote.

- Honest limits: HireWire doesn’t detect the language of a posting. Use blocked keywords to push German-only roles down (below), and check each posting’s language requirements.

## Which feeds have jobs in Germany

HireWire reads public job feeds straight from your browser. For Germany, the useful ones are:

- Company career pages of employers headquartered in Germany: N26, Trade Republic, Raisin, Delivery Hero, HelloFresh, GetYourGuide, Contentful, Enpal, n8n and Thermondo (Berlin), Celonis, Helsing and SIXT (Munich area), DeepL (Cologne), Bosch (Stuttgart area), 1KOMMA5° (Hamburg) and Chrono24 (Karlsruhe). Many of these companies hire for roles where English is the working language; the posting says which.

- International companies with offices in Germany whose global boards are in the feed list, so their German roles appear alongside the rest.

- Arbeitnow, a job board focused on Germany and Europe.

- Remote boards (Remotive, Jobicy, RemoteOK, We Work Remotely, Hacker News “Who is hiring?”), for remote roles open to people living in Germany or the EU.

- Optional, with your own free key: Adzuna (country: Germany) adds a much larger set of German postings. Your key stays in your browser.

The full source list and how the feeds are read are in the guide (https://hirewire.fyi/guide.html).

## How to find English-speaking roles in Germany with HireWire

- Set your role and place. Open HireWire, enter your skills (or build a CV (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html) and hand it over in one click), the city you want and whether you want remote, hybrid or on-site.

- Set a salary floor in EUR. Postings that list pay below it drop down the list; many German postings list no pay at all, which costs a few points rather than hiding them.

- Push German-only roles down. Add blocked keywords such as fließend Deutsch, Deutschkenntnisse, verhandlungssicher or German C1. Each match lowers a posting’s score sharply, so roles that require German sink to the bottom while still being visible.

- Hide what you can’t take. Blocked locations remove postings from places you won’t move to.

- Check the posting. Before applying, read the language requirements, and look at the ghost-job risk (https://hirewire.fyi/ghost-job-checker.html) and the salary check (https://hirewire.fyi/salary-checker.html).

## What HireWire won’t do

- It doesn’t show every job in Germany. StepStone, Indeed and LinkedIn are not feeds (see StepStone oder Indeed? (https://hirewire.fyi/de/stepstone-indeed-linkedin-jobs-bewerten.html), in German).

- It doesn’t include the Bundesagentur für Arbeit job search.

- It doesn’t translate postings or detect their language, and its interface is in English.

## Applying in Germany: the CV question

For international and English-speaking teams, a one-page or two-page English CV without a photo is usually fine. More traditional German employers often expect a tabular Lebenslauf, sometimes with a photo, which is common but not required. The free CV builder (https://hirewire.fyi/cv-builder.html) does both: three ATS-friendly English templates and a German Lebenslauf (German version (https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-vorlage.html)), PDF download, no sign-up, and your CV stays in your browser.

## FAQ

**Q: Is there a job aggregator for English-speaking jobs in Germany?**

HireWire is a free one: it combines 55 public job feeds, including career pages of German employers and Arbeitnow, a Germany-focused board, into one list ranked by your skills. It doesn’t filter by posting language, so use blocked keywords such as “fließend Deutsch” to push German-only roles down.

**Q: Do I need an account?**

No. HireWire has no accounts. Your profile, saved jobs and notes stay in your browser’s storage on your device.

**Q: Is it free?**

Yes. The feeds, ranking, tracker, ghost-job and salary checks and the CV builder are free. Only the optional AI fit score is paid after 3 free scores: a one-time pass from €9, no subscription.

**Q: Does HireWire include StepStone, Indeed or LinkedIn jobs?**

No. Those sites don’t offer public feeds HireWire can read. A browser extension that scores postings on them is built but not yet published.

**Q: Can I find remote jobs from Germany?**

Yes. Several feeds are remote job boards; set “remote” in your profile and use blocked locations to hide roles restricted to countries you can’t work from.

Title: HireWire auf Deutsch – Jobsuche ohne Datenkrake, kostenlos und ohne Konto

HireWire auf Deutsch

# Jobsuche ohne Datenkrake

HireWire findet Stellen für dich, bewertet sie nach deinem Profil und verwaltet deine Bewerbungen. Ohne Konto, ohne Abo, und deine Bewerbungsdaten liegen nicht auf unserem Server, sondern in deinem Browser.

HireWire · zuletzt geprüft am 21.10.2026

Neu: Lebenslauf-Vorlage kostenlos
Tabellarischer Lebenslauf oder drei ATS-freundliche Vorlagen. PDF-Download ohne Anmeldung, ohne Wasserzeichen, dein Lebenslauf bleibt im Browser.

Lebenslauf erstellen → (https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-vorlage.html)

▶ 90-Sek.-Demo ansehen (https://hirewire.fyi/assets/video/hirewire-demo-16x9.mp4)

Was ist HireWire? Ein kostenloser Job-Feed-Aggregator und Bewerbungstracker, der lokal in deinem Browser läuft: 55 öffentliche Job-Feeds in einer Liste, sortiert nach einem nachvollziehbaren Match-Score. Kein Konto, deine Daten bleiben in deinem Browser. Optionale KI-Pässe ab 9 €.

## Kurz gesagt

- Kein Konto, keine Nutzerdatenbank. Profil, Lebenslauf-Stichworte, Bewerbungen, Notizen und Kontakte speichert dein Browser, nicht HireWire.

- Stellen kommen zu dir. 55 öffentliche Job-Feeds in einer Liste, stündlich aktualisiert und nach deinen Skills, deinem Mindestgehalt und deinen Ausschlusswörtern sortiert.

- Weniger Zeit für Phantom-Stellen. Jede Anzeige bekommt ein Ghost-Job-Risiko (https://hirewire.fyi/de/ghost-jobs-erkennen.html) mit Begründung.

- Ehrlich: Die App selbst ist noch auf Englisch, und die Feeds sind stark auf Remote- und Tech-Jobs ausgerichtet, enthalten aber auch deutsche Arbeitgeber wie N26, Celonis, Trade Republic, Delivery Hero, SIXT und Bosch.

## Was „ohne Datenkrake“ konkret heißt

Viele Bewerbungstools speichern deine komplette Jobsuche in ihrer Cloud: wo du dich beworben hast, deine Notizen, deinen Lebenslauf. HireWire funktioniert anders. Es gibt keine Anmeldung und keine Datenbank mit Nutzerinnen und Nutzern. Alles, was du eingibst, liegt im Speicher deines Browsers (localStorage, gespiegelt in IndexedDB). Eine Sicherung ist eine einzige JSON-Datei, die du selbst aufbewahrst.

Damit das Versprechen auch einem Blick in die Entwicklertools standhält, hier die Ausnahmen:

- Job-Feeds: Dein Browser ruft die öffentlichen Feeds (z. B. Remotive, Arbeitnow, Greenhouse) direkt ab. Die sehen dabei deine IP-Adresse, aber keine Profildaten.

- Optionaler KI-Fit-Score: Nur wenn du auf „Score with AI“ klickst, gehen dein Lebenslauf-Text und diese eine Anzeige an HireWires Bewertungsfunktion und weiter an Googles Gemini-API (kostenpflichtige Stufe). Sie werden nicht gespeichert.

- Nutzungsstatistik: Die App zählt cookielos, welche Funktionen genutzt werden (PostHog), nie Jobtitel, Suchbegriffe oder Lebenslauf. Bei aktivem „Do Not Track“ läuft sie gar nicht. Diese Ratgeber-Seiten laden keine Statistik.

Alle Details stehen in der Datenschutz-Kurzfassung (https://hirewire.fyi/de/datenschutz.html) und vollständig auf Englisch auf der Privacy-Seite (https://hirewire.fyi/privacy.html).

## Was HireWire kann

- Stellen finden: sechs Jobbörsen (darunter Arbeitnow mit Stellen in Europa, auch in Deutschland) und 49 Karriereseiten von Firmen wie Stripe, N26 oder Bosch. Mit einem kostenlosen Adzuna-Schlüssel kommen Stellen aus Deutschland und zwölf weiteren Ländern dazu.

- Bewerten: ein nachvollziehbarer Match-Score aus Skills, Gehalt, Aktualität und Remote-Option, dazu Ghost-Job-Risiko und ein Gehalts-Check aus den Anzeigen in deinen Feeds.

- Lebenslauf: eine kostenlose Lebenslauf-Vorlage (https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-vorlage.html) (tabellarisch oder ATS-freundlich, PDF), die deinen Lebenslauf mit einem Klick an die App übergibt.

- Verwalten: eine Pipeline von „gemerkt“ bis „Angebot“, mit Notizen, Kontakten, Terminen und Follow-up-Erinnerungen samt E-Mail-Entwurf (auf Englisch).

- Optional mit KI: Googles KI-Modell Gemini bewertet deinen Lebenslauf für eine Stelle von 0 bis 10 und nennt die wichtigsten Verbesserungen. 3 Bewertungen sind kostenlos, danach gibt es einen einmaligen Pass (9 € für 7 Tage, 19 € für 30 Tage) ohne Abo. Pass Plus (29 € für 30 Tage) schreibt außerdem Anschreiben, Lebenslauf-Entwürfe, Gesprächsvorbereitung und Verhandlungsskripte.

- Auf mehreren Geräten: Mit jedem Pass kannst du deine Daten Ende-zu-Ende-verschlüsselt synchronisieren. Den Schlüssel hast nur du.

- Als App installieren: HireWire lässt sich auf Handy oder Desktop installieren und startet dann auch offline.

## Was HireWire (noch) nicht kann

- eine deutsche Oberfläche: Die App ist auf Englisch.

- Stellen von StepStone, Indeed oder LinkedIn übernehmen: Eine Browser-Erweiterung dafür ist gebaut, aber bald verfügbar. Mehr dazu (https://hirewire.fyi/de/stepstone-indeed-linkedin-jobs-bewerten.html).

- Bewerbungen von Hand eintragen: Getrackt werden Stellen aus den Feeds. Für alles andere hilft unsere Excel-Vorlage (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungen-verwalten-excel-vorlage.html).

## Kostenlose Tools und Ratgeber

- Lebenslauf-Vorlage kostenlos (https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-vorlage.html): tabellarisch oder ATS-freundlich ausfüllen, als PDF herunterladen, ohne Anmeldung.

- Ghost Jobs erkennen (https://hirewire.fyi/de/ghost-jobs-erkennen.html): Anzeige einfügen, Risiko sehen. Direkt im Browser.

- Bewerbungstracker kostenlos (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungstracker-kostenlos.html): welche Optionen es gibt und was sie mit deinen Daten machen.

- Bewerbungen verwalten mit Excel (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungen-verwalten-excel-vorlage.html): kostenlose Vorlage zum Herunterladen.

- Lebenslauf ATS-freundlich schreiben (https://hirewire.fyi/de/lebenslauf-ats-tipps.html): was Bewerbermanagementsysteme lesen können und was nicht.

- Salary checker (https://hirewire.fyi/salary-checker.html) (Englisch): Gehälter aus aktuellen Remote-Anzeigen.

## Häufige Fragen

**Q: Ist HireWire wirklich kostenlos?**

Ja. Feeds, Bewertung, Pipeline, Ghost-Job-Risiko, Gehalts-Check und Exporte sind kostenlos und ohne Konto. Kostenpflichtig ist nur der optionale KI-Fit-Score nach 3 freien Bewertungen, als einmaliger Pass ohne Abo, oder kostenlos mit deinem eigenen Anthropic-API-Schlüssel.

**Q: Gibt es HireWire auf Deutsch?**

Diese Ratgeber-Seiten sind auf Deutsch, die App selbst ist derzeit auf Englisch. Sie rechnet aber mit Euro-Gehältern, zeigt Stellen in Deutschland, und ein Teil der Prüfungen versteht auch deutsche Anzeigentexte.

**Q: Wo werden meine Daten gespeichert?**

Im Speicher deines Browsers auf deinem Gerät. HireWire hat keine Konten und keinen Server, auf dem deine Bewerbungen liegen. Mach regelmäßig eine Sicherung, denn wenn du die Website-Daten löschst, sind sie weg.

**Q: Finde ich bei HireWire Jobs in Deutschland?**

Einige: Arbeitnow und mehrere Firmen-Karriereseiten haben Stellen in Deutschland, viele Feeds sind aber international und remote. Mit einem kostenlosen Adzuna-Schlüssel (Land: Germany) wird die Auswahl deutlich größer.

**Q: Warum nicht einfach Stellen in ChatGPT einfügen?**

Für eine Stelle geht das. HireWire ist für die anderen 200 gebaut. Es findet die Stellen: 55 öffentliche Feeds und Firmen-Karriereseiten in einer Liste, ohne Kopieren und Einfügen. Es prüft jede Anzeige automatisch und kostenlos (deine Skills, dein Mindestgehalt, gesperrte Begriffe und Orte, dazu Ghost-Job- und Gehalts-Hinweise), während ein Chatbot nur die Anzeige sieht, die du ihm gibst. Es merkt sich alles: gespeichert, beworben, Gespräch und Angebot auf einem Board, mit Erinnerungen und Exporten statt in alten Chatverläufen. Es ist von Haus aus privat: kein Konto, Board und Lebenslauf bleiben in deinem Browser, und Text verlässt dein Gerät nur, wenn du einen KI-Fit-Score anforderst. Und es ist günstiger für die Jobsuche: kostenlos, oder eine Woche KI-Bewertungen für 9 € statt eines monatlichen Chatbot-Abos. Nutze ChatGPT zum Feinschliff deines Anschreibens und HireWire, um zu entscheiden, welche Stellen eines verdienen.

URL: https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungstracker-kostenlos.html
Title: Bewerbungstracker kostenlos: Optionen im Vergleich (ohne Konto möglich)

Ratgeber

# Bewerbungstracker kostenlos: welche Option passt zu dir?

Spätestens wenn mehrere Bewerbungen gleichzeitig laufen, hilft ein System. Kostenlos geht das auf mehrere Arten, und sie unterscheiden sich vor allem darin, wer am Ende deine Daten hat.

HireWire · zuletzt geprüft am 15.10.2026

## Kurz gesagt

- Volle Kontrolle, alles von Hand: eine Tabelle. Unsere kostenlose Excel-Vorlage (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungen-verwalten-excel-vorlage.html) ist ein guter Start.

- Bequem, mit KI-Lebenslauf, Daten in der Cloud: Huntr oder Teal, jeweils mit Konto.

- Stellen finden und verwalten ohne Konto: HireWire. Deine Daten bleiben im Browser, die App ist auf Englisch.

## Was ein Bewerbungstracker leisten sollte

- Status auf einen Blick: gemerkt, beworben, Gespräch, Angebot, Absage.

- Termine und Nachfassen: Wann hast du dich beworben, wann solltest du nachhaken?

- Kontakte und Notizen pro Stelle, damit du vor dem Gespräch nicht suchen musst.

- Export: Deine Daten sollten sich jederzeit als Datei mitnehmen lassen.

- Datenschutz: Eine Jobsuche ist sensibel, besonders wenn du noch angestellt bist. Wer speichert die Liste, und unter welchem Konto?

## Die kostenlosen Optionen im Vergleich

| | Excel / Google Sheets | HireWire | Huntr (Free) | Teal (Free) |

| Kosten | kostenlos | kostenlos; optionaler KI-Pass einmalig 9 € / 19 € | kostenlos bis 100 Jobs; Pro 40 $ pro Monat | kostenlos; Teal+ ab 13 $ pro Woche |

| Konto nötig | bei Google Sheets ja, bei Excel lokal nein | nein | ja | ja |

| Wo die Daten liegen | in deiner Datei bzw. deinem Cloud-Speicher | in deinem Browser | Huntr-Cloud | Teal-Konto (Cloud) |

| Stellen eintragen | von Hand | aus 55 Feeds; StepStone, Indeed, LinkedIn per Erweiterung bald verfügbar | Chrome-Clipper | Chrome-Erweiterung |

| Erinnerungen | selbst bauen | Follow-up-Plan mit E-Mail-Entwürfen und Kalenderdatei | nicht geprüft | E-Mail-Vorlagen je Phase |

| Sprache | deine | Englisch | Englisch | Englisch |

Angaben zu Huntr und Teal von deren Preis- und Produktseiten, Stand 15.10.2026. Preise in US-Dollar, Änderungen vorbehalten. HireWire veröffentlicht diese Seite.

## Tabelle: der ehrliche Klassiker

Eine Tabelle kann alles, was du ihr beibringst, und gehört dir. Der Preis ist Handarbeit: Stellen kopieren, Status pflegen, Nachfass-Termine selbst im Blick behalten. Für eine überschaubare Suche reicht das völlig. In unserer Vorlage (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungen-verwalten-excel-vorlage.html) sind Status-Auswahl, Fälligkeits-Markierung und eine kleine Auswertung schon eingebaut.

## Cloud-Tools: bequem, aber mit Konto

Huntr und Teal sind ausgereifte Plattformen mit Browser-Erweiterung, Lebenslauf-Editor und KI-Funktionen. Dafür legst du ein Konto an, und deine Jobsuche liegt auf deren Servern. Bei Huntr endet der kostenlose Plan bei 100 getrackten Jobs, bei Teal ist das Tracking kostenlos unbegrenzt, KI-Funktionen sind im Gratis-Plan aber begrenzt.

## HireWire: finden, bewerten, verwalten, ohne Konto

HireWire ist eher Job-Radar als Formular: Es zeigt dir laufend Stellen aus 55 öffentlichen Quellen, sortiert nach deinem Profil, mit Ghost-Job-Risiko (https://hirewire.fyi/de/ghost-jobs-erkennen.html) und Gehalts-Check. Was dich interessiert, legst du in die Pipeline. Alles bleibt im Browser; eine JSON-Datei sichert den kompletten Stand.

Die Grenzen: Die Oberfläche ist Englisch, die Feeds sind vor allem Remote- und Tech-Stellen, und Bewerbungen außerhalb der Feeds kannst du (noch) nicht eintragen. Viele kombinieren deshalb HireWire mit einer Tabelle.

## Häufige Fragen

**Q: Welcher Bewerbungstracker ist kostenlos und ohne Anmeldung?**

Eine lokale Excel-Datei und HireWire. HireWire läuft im Browser ohne Konto und speichert deine Daten nur auf deinem Gerät.

**Q: Ist eine Excel-Tabelle als Bewerbungstracker ausreichend?**

Für viele ja. Sie ist flexibel und gehört dir. Nachteile sind die Handarbeit und fehlende Erinnerungen. Unsere Vorlage (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungen-verwalten-excel-vorlage.html) markiert immerhin fällige Termine automatisch.

**Q: Sind meine Daten bei HireWire DSGVO-sicher?**

HireWire speichert deine Bewerbungsdaten nicht auf einem Server, sondern in deinem Browser. Was trotzdem übertragen wird (z. B. beim optionalen KI-Fit-Score), steht in der Datenschutz-Kurzfassung (https://hirewire.fyi/de/datenschutz.html). Eine rechtliche Bewertung ersetzt das nicht.

**Q: Kann ich von Huntr oder Teal zu HireWire wechseln?**

Ja, aber ohne Import: HireWire kann keine Daten aus anderen Trackern übernehmen. Lass die alten Bewerbungen dort oder in einer Tabelle und nutze HireWire für neue Stellen.

Title: Bewerbungen verwalten mit Excel: kostenlose Vorlage (XLSX & CSV)

Vorlage zum Download

# Bewerbungen verwalten mit Excel: kostenlose Vorlage

Eine Zeile pro Stelle, Status per Auswahlliste, fällige Termine werden rot. Ohne Makros, ohne Anmeldung, ohne E-Mail-Adresse.

HireWire · zuletzt geprüft am 15.10.2026

Bewerbungs-Tracker-Vorlage
XLSX, 3 Blätter (Bewerbungen, Auswertung, Anleitung), 200 Zeilen vorformatiert. Läuft in Excel, LibreOffice und Google Sheets.

Vorlage herunterladen (.xlsx) (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungs-tracker-vorlage.xlsx)
Nur Spalten (.csv) (https://hirewire.fyi/de/bewerbungs-tracker-vorlage.csv)

## Was in der Vorlage steckt

- 15 Spalten: Firma, Stelle, Ort, Arbeitsmodell, Quelle, Link zur Anzeige, Gehalt laut Anzeige, Status, Beworben am, Nächster Schritt, Fällig am, Ansprechperson, E-Mail, Ghost-Risiko, Notizen.

- Auswahllisten für Status (Gemerkt, Beworben, Telefoninterview, Vorstellungsgespräch, Angebot, Zusage, Absage, Zurückgezogen, Keine Antwort), Arbeitsmodell und Ghost-Risiko.

- Fälligkeits-Markierung: Ist „Fällig am“ heute oder vorbei, wird die Zelle rot, solange die Bewerbung noch offen ist. Abgeschlossene Zeilen werden grau.

- Auswertung: Anzahl je Status, Gesamtzahl, fällige Termine und Gespräche, per Formel, ganz ohne Makros.

- Kopfzeile und erste zwei Spalten bleiben beim Scrollen stehen, Filter sind gesetzt. Zwei erfundene Beispielzeilen zeigen, wie es aussieht; lösch sie einfach.

Die CSV-Datei enthält nur Spalten und Beispielzeilen (Trennzeichen Semikolon, UTF-8), ohne Auswahllisten und Formatierung. Sie ist für Numbers, Notion oder andere Tools gedacht, die CSV importieren.

## So nutzt du die Vorlage gut

- Eine Zeile pro Stelle, auch für Stellen, die du dir nur merkst. So siehst du später, woher die guten Gespräche kamen (Spalte Quelle).

- Immer einen nächsten Schritt mit Datum eintragen: nachfassen, Gesprächstermin, Frist. Die rote Markierung zeigt dir morgens, was heute dran ist.

- Gehalt so notieren, wie es in der Anzeige steht. Fehlt es, bleibt das Feld leer; das ist für die spätere Verhandlung auch eine Information.

- Verdächtige Anzeigen prüfen, bevor du Zeit in ein Anschreiben steckst: mit unserem Ghost-Job-Check (https://hirewire.fyi/de/ghost-jobs-erkennen.html), und das Ergebnis in die Spalte Ghost-Risiko übernehmen.

- Datei sichern: Sie liegt dort, wo du sie speicherst. Bei Google Sheets ist das dein Google-Konto.

## Wann eine Tabelle nicht mehr reicht

Die Tabelle ist ehrlich und flexibel. Mühsam wird sie, wenn du viele Stellen sichtest: Anzeigen kopieren, Duplikate erkennen, an Nachfass-Termine denken, Gehälter vergleichen. Genau dafür gibt es HireWire (https://hirewire.fyi/de/):

| | Excel-Vorlage | HireWire |

| Stellen finden | selbst suchen und abtippen | 55 öffentliche Job-Feeds, stündlich aktualisiert, nach deinem Profil sortiert |

| Stellen eintragen | jede, von Hand | nur Stellen aus den Feeds; StepStone, Indeed und LinkedIn per Erweiterung bald verfügbar |

| Nachfassen | Datum selbst eintragen | automatischer Follow-up-Plan mit E-Mail-Entwurf (Englisch) und Kalenderdatei |

| Ghost Jobs | Spalte zum Selbst-Eintragen | Risiko für jede Anzeige, mit Begründung |

| Gehalt | notieren | Median und Spanne aus den Anzeigen in deinen Feeds |

| Daten | deine Datei | dein Browser, kein Konto, Sicherung als JSON-Datei |

| Kosten | kostenlos | kostenlos; optionaler KI-Fit-Score: 3 frei, dann einmalig 9 € oder 19 € |

Viele nutzen beides: HireWire für das Finden und Bewerten, die Tabelle für Bewerbungen, die über Kontakte oder Personalvermittler laufen.

## Häufige Fragen

**Q: Ist die Excel-Vorlage wirklich kostenlos?**

Ja. Kein Konto, keine E-Mail-Adresse, keine Makros. Du kannst sie frei verwenden und anpassen.

**Q: Funktioniert die Vorlage in Google Sheets oder LibreOffice?**

Ja. Lade die XLSX-Datei in Google Drive hoch oder öffne sie in LibreOffice Calc. Auswahllisten, Markierungen und Formeln funktionieren dort ebenfalls.

**Q: Warum wird ein Datum rot?**

Die Spalte „Fällig am“ wird rot, wenn das Datum heute oder in der Vergangenheit liegt und die Bewerbung nicht abgeschlossen ist (Status nicht Absage, Zusage oder Zurückgezogen).

**Q: Kann ich die Tabelle in HireWire importieren?**

Nein. HireWire kann keine Tabellen importieren und trackt nur Stellen aus seinen Feeds. Behalte die Tabelle für alles andere.
